title: Q/C boundary: out-of-scope fcmp predicate (one/ueq/ord/uno/...) silently mints a non-existent template symbol (verify-clean miscompile)
description:
DISCOVERED during ziov.4 Rule-13 adversarial review (2026-06-15), confirmed by repro. A tainted data-position fcmp with an OUT-OF-SCOPE predicate (anything outside {oeq,une,olt,ogt,ole,oge} — i.e. one/ord/uno/ueq/ugt/uge/ult/ule/true/false) is lowered with NO scope check: CompareLowering::lowerCompareImpl computes the predicate name and width, then WidthDispatch::compareTemplateFn does an unconditional getOrInsertFunction(compareName(...)) which is NEVER null. There is no predicate-scope gate anywhere in the pass (no compareInScope analogous to castInScope; TaintPropagation/OpcodeLowering collect every tainted CmpInst regardless of predicate). 

RESULT: the pass emits a call to a runtime template that DOES NOT EXIST (the YAML ships only 6 fcmp preds — tools/opcode_table.yaml:83 'fcmp: [oeq, une, olt, ogt, ole, oge]'; runtime/cq_templates.c has only those). opt exits 0, opt -verify is clean, and the program fails at Stage-3 LINK with an undefined symbol — a verify-clean miscompile (the project's unforgivable class, Rule 1 fail-loud violated).

CONFIRMED REPROS (exit 0, bogus symbol minted):
1. STRAIGHT-LINE (no control flow, pre-existing & independent of ziov.4): 
   %a = call float @cq_theta_f32(float 2.0, double 0.5); %c = fcmp one float %a, 1.0; %m = call i1 @cq_measure_i1(i1 %c)
   -> mints 'call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_one_f32_hl(i32 %h, float 1.0)', exit 0, NO diagnostic.
2. COND-DATA-USE LINEAGE (mutate-then-fail; the ziov.4 detect-before-mutate family, NOT closed by ziov.4's cast-only gate): 
   %c=icmp sgt %q,5; %f=uitofp i1 %c to float (IN SCOPE); %g=fcmp one float %f,0.0 (OUT OF SCOPE); br %c ...
   -> condDataUseDisposition walks %c->%f(cast,ok)->%g(CmpInst, NO pred gate)->ShareOk; emitRegion ROUTES (cqrt_cswap emitted) + flattenRegion erases the diamond, THEN mints the bogus fcmp symbol. exit 0.

REACHABILITY: clang -O1 emits oeq/une/olt/ogt/ole/oge for C float ==,!=,<,>,<=,>= (all in scope). The out-of-scope preds arise from __builtin_isunordered, NaN-aware idioms (a<b||a>b -> one), or non-default fast-math. Uncommon but not synthetic-only; the project rule is decline-loud-never-silent regardless of frequency (Prime Directive).

FIX (recommended, mirrors castInScope): add compareInScope(StringRef op, StringRef predName, StringRef width) to OpcodeSupport (icmp: all 10 preds; fcmp: {oeq,une,olt,ogt,ole,oge}). Consult it in (a) CompareLowering::lowerCompareImpl/rewriteCompare -> diagnoseNoTemplate + return null (loud, leaves cmp standing, verify-clean) for the STRAIGHT-LINE root; and (b) ArmClassify::condDataUseDisposition CmpInst branch -> return CondDataDisp::Unlowerable for the cond-data-use DETECT-BEFORE-MUTATE half. Core lowering change -> Rule-13 adversarial review + red-green decline fixtures (straight-line negative + cond-data-use negative).
close_reason: compareInScope(op,pred) predicate-scope gate added to OpcodeSupport; consulted at 4 sites — CompareLowering::lowerCompareImpl (universal silent-mint backstop, fwd/_inv/QQ/HL), condDataUseDisposition CmpInst branch, classifyArms flat control cond, recoverRegionTree nested outer+inner. Out-of-scope fcmp now declines LOUDLY pre-mutation instead of minting a non-existent symbol. Rule-13 cleared by independent review (verified empirically). 4 red-green fixtures. icmp unaffected (all 10 in scope).

title: Taint-escape: opaque user call consuming a tainted value in a NON-angle position silently reads the runtime handle tag after RAUW
description: Discovered during test_C_libtooling-659 review (2026-06-10). The 659 fix closed the ANGLE-slot family, but an opaque user call consuming a tainted value in a non-angle, non-intrinsic position (e.g. 'int r = ext(q); ...' where @ext is an external double/int fn and the result feeds DATA, not a rotation angle) survives lowering well-typed: after RotationLowering's RAUW the call reads the i32 RUNTIME HANDLE TAG — verify-clean, links, runs, plausible trace = the silent-miscompile class. The cross-type-RAUW instance of this family fails loudly at the verifier (documented in CastLowering.cpp audit comment, 832ddc4), but the same-typed instance is silent. Root fix candidate: TaintPropagation or a dedicated guard should loudly decline any UNKNOWN (non-cq_*, non-lowerable) call that consumes a tainted SSA value — the taint discipline only knows how to lower stock opcodes and cq intrinsics; an opaque callee is an unproven shape (Prime Directive: decline). Rule 12: ship with straight-line reject fixtures (same-typed opaque consumer; also check a tainted value passed as an argument deeper in a call chain). Audit: are there OTHER non-call escapes (store to global/escaped alloca, ptrtoint, va_arg)?
notes: WORKER (2026-06-10): Root fix landed as TaintPropagation::declineTaintEscapes — pure analysis, wired FIRST in BOTH pipeline entry points (run + runOnFunction, twin-pipeline trap), pre-RAUW. Design: known-consumer allowlist (collected theta/phi/measure call sites by EXACT CallInst membership — never name-prefix on the accept side; cqrt_*/cq_template_* defensive; cq_invert_* = FreePoint's recognized Phase-7 escape; the 4 lowerOps classes; phi/select; terminators incl. ret) — EVERYTHING else reading a tainted value declines loudly. 3 messages: 'unknown callee' (opaque extern, in-module body [Phase 6 clone-on-taint NOT implemented — visible body declines identically, fixture pins the boundary], llvm.* intrinsics, indirect), 'stored to memory', 'unsupported instruction' (GEP/atomics/freeze/... decline-by-default). Audit results: inttoptr already LOUD (CastLowering 'no template'); ret = recognized Escaped (FreePoint, pinned ACCEPT fixtures); va_arg unreachable as direct user (varargs CALL covered by unknown-callee); classical-cond select/phi over tainted data left with ControlDetect/FreePoint (note: FreePoint's net is bypassed when handle is ALSO measured — Measured returns before FirstUnrecognized — my guard covers store/GEP/call instances of that hole; select/phi instance remains, see open question). 6 new reject fixtures lowering_reject_taint_escape_*; 4 angle fixtures re-shaped/re-pointed (opt exits at FIRST DS_Error, so the earlier-firing escape guard owns the @ext producer shapes; sitofp producers keep angle-guard coverage). Full ctest 9/9 green.

title: Pre-existing: dead arm-local cq_phi on a mux base lowers to an unbalanced in-arm controlled Rz
description:
ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW FINDING (u5f review, 2026-06-03), PRE-EXISTING (byte-identical old-vs-new — NOT introduced by u5f's G2/G3 widening). In a distinct-base MUX-EXCH gated switch, a DEAD arm-local cq_phi applied to a mux base q (a gate body in q's selecting arm whose RESULT is not what the mux φ edge carries) is collected into the arm's Gate shadow and lowered by substituteArm to an in-arm cqrt_rz_<W>_controlled(f_q, q, angle). The npu.6/u5f uncompute (emitChainInv) inverts only the UNCONDITIONAL prep chain (2-arg cqrt_ry/cqrt_rz with arg0==q), NOT this 3-arg controlled in-arm Rz — so on the SELECTED path q carries an extra Rz that the cswap moves into regOut (intended for real gate bodies) but if the cq_phi result is DEAD (not the φ-carried value) the Rz is stray, leaving regOut with an uncompensated rotation. G3b (per-arm correspondence) checks that a gate on q lives in a q-SELECTING arm but does NOT check that the gate's result is actually THREADED to the merge φ (vs a dead local). Needs its own adversarial review to (a) confirm reproducibility on a concrete fixture and (b) decide fix: tighten G3b to require the gate body's result reach the mux φ edge (resolveGatedHandleBase of the φ incoming == the gate, not just == its base), OR decline a mux arm containing a dead base-mutating gate. Probe label 'p2' in the u5f review. Over-decline is always safe. See docs/npu6-mux-exch-gate-spec.md §3 (G3a/G3b) + [[mux-exch-gate-per-arm-correspondence]].

## Context
Surfaced while implementing u5f (G2/G3 multi-op Bennett uncompute). Reviewer classified it pre-existing and out-of-scope for u5f; filed for a future hardening pass, mirroring how the shared-merge UAF (ehf) was split out of 5bl.
notes: RESOLVED — NOT A BUG (investigated 2026-06-03, empirical + independent adversarial verification). The hazard requires NON-LINEAR handle use (a no-cloning violation): a 'dead' cq_phi on mux base q whose result is not threaded to the φ needs q used twice off the same SSA value, which a well-formed linear program (CQ.h frontend; a truly dead/leaked handle is itself a linearity violation) cannot produce. Empirically a non-linear dead-clone arm lowers BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the well-formed linear two-gate arm (in-place handle model RAUWs {q, cq_phi(q,.), .} to one handle, so both cq_phi become two cqrt_rz on the one register = the valid linear interpretation; the 'extra' Rz is only extra under the non-physical cloning reading). The cswap captures all in-arm gates before the move and the non-selected uncompute IS balanced. Adversarial verifier (10 probe categories: linear chains, shared/folded arms, cross-block preps, default/direct-default, chained-theta+gate, measure/return escapes, crash sweep) found ZERO accepted-and-miscompiled inputs; every genuine cross-arm hazard is over-declined by G3b (_wrongarmmut*) and every cross-φ/post-merge cloning hazard by G6 (_crossphi_alias, _postmergelive). NOTE: a general IR-level no-cloning/linearity CHECKER is out of scope by design — the spec §1 establishes correctness by-construction on linear well-formed input, with the frontend guaranteeing linearity and specific cloning shapes declined (G6). Locked the well-formed sibling shape with lowering_control_switch_gated_distinct_multigatearm.ll.
close_reason: Closed

title: Non-selected-source uncompute for MUX-EXCH (Bennett/QROM disentangle)
description: Sub-task (iii) of npu.1, the HARD part flagged 'real design work — spike it'. controlled-SWAP frees only the SELECTED source per branch; NON-selected sources retain prepared state ENTANGLED with the scrutinee s (garbage that pollutes regOut's measurement). Reverse each non-selected source's prep in its branch (Bennett / QROM MUX-EXCH uncomputation). Spike the design first.
acceptance_criteria: MUX-EXCH lowering disentangles non-selected sources so regOut's measurement is correct across all scrutinee values (not just the selected branch); demonstrated end-to-end (clang -O1 -> cq-lowering -> verify) on the distinct-handle multiplexer.
notes:
SPIKE FINDINGS (2026-06-03). PREREQUISITE BLOCKER: uncomputing a source's cq_theta (Ry) prep needs cqrt_ry_<W>_controlled_inv — the runtime has ONLY cqrt_rz_<W>_controlled_inv. Add 7 widths (i1/i8/i16/i32/i64/f32/f64) in runtime/cq_runtime.{h,c} + a ControlledSymbols accessor (mirror controlledRotationFn) FIRST. PLAN (direct-cq_theta case): for each base handle q, uncompute its prep on the branches where q is NON-selected — controlled on ¬f_q (= OR of the OTHER handles' selection flags) — by emitting cqrt_ry_<W>_controlled_inv(¬f_q, q, angle). Recover <angle> from the already-lowered cqrt_ry call on q (rotation lowering runs BEFORE controlled lowering, so the cq_theta is gone — scan for the cqrt_ry whose handle is q). GENERAL CASE (the 'spike it' part, UNSOLVED): a source with a multi-op prep history, a chained theta, or live out-of-region uses can't be naively reversed (Bennett/QROM-MUX-EXCH). TIGHTLY GATE: only lower when every base handle is a single direct cqrt_ry prep with no out-of-region uses; else decline (npu.1 path) — over-decline-safe. CANNOT be correctness-validated in the trace-only runtime (structural fixtures only).
GATE SPEC WRITTEN: docs/npu6-mux-exch-gate-spec.md (adversarial design review 2026-06-03, 6 attackers + synth). REFRAME (confirmed): uncompute correctness is a unitarity theorem (U†U=I) validated by construction + gate-sequence fixtures like every other gate — NOT a simulator gap. The whole risk is the GATE admitting an unsafe case. Spec defines an 8-layer CONSERVATIVE gate G0-G7 (decline on any failure): G0 npu.1 structure/identity; G1 base is a direct cq_theta (not select/phi/arg/data-op); G2 single-Ry (classical arg0, reject chained theta); G3 no extra mutation between prep and merge (reject theta-then-cq_phi Rz garbage); G4 no direct-to-merge default for a distinct-base mux phi; G5 variable-angle dominance; G6 cross-phi base disjointness + region-wide LIVENESS (no-cloning / dead-after-merge — this absorbs the liveness angle); G7 uniform width across mux bases. Plus prerequisites (the 7 cqrt_ry_*_controlled_inv + WidthDispatch resolver + DominatorTree), the ATOMIC-LANDING requirement (gate+mux+uncompute+symbols are one indivisible commit, else revert to the npu.1 decline), the narrow happy-path that lowers, impl order, the positive+decline+regression fixtures, and 4 open risks. See the doc.
close_reason: Non-selected-source uncompute landed atomically with npu.5. Per-non-selected base cqrt_ry_<W>_controlled_inv(NOT f_q,q,angle) (7 ry inverse runtime symbols + ControlledSymbols::controlledRyInvFn). Angle recovered from lowered cqrt_ry (recoverRyAngle); width from taint.HandleWidth. Adversarial review confirmed algebra correct for 2/3/4/5-base; found+fixed C1 (G3b per-arm correspondence silent-miscompile). Spec G3b updated; regression fixtures wrongarmmut{,_default}.

title: MUX-EXCH gated-switch lowering + detection routing (distinct per-case handles)
description: Sub-task (ii) of npu.1. Replace the interim decline (resolveGatedHandleBase same-base-handle check in tryBuildGatedSwitchRegion) with correct MUX-EXCH lowering: regOut = cqrt_alloc(0); for each DISTINCT base handle q, cqrt_cswap([OR of that arm's case eq-flags], regOut, q); RAUW merge φ -> regOut. Per-arm controlled gates stay as today (applied before the move). Mixed/classical arms reuse the dissolveSelect add/sub seed. Route the distinct-base-handle merge φ (detected by the discriminator) to this lowering instead of declining; uniform-handle merges keep the cheap RAUW.
acceptance_criteria: POSITIVE fixture lowering_control_switch_gated_distinct.ll flipped to assert cqrt_cswap-based MUX-EXCH: fresh cqrt_alloc + per-arm controlled-SWAP, no dropped edge, downstream uses the muxed register, opt -verify clean, result correct per scrutinee. Uniform-handle gated fixtures byte-identical.
notes:
SPIKE FINDINGS (2026-06-03; npu.4 landed cqrt_cswap + ControlledSymbols::cswapFn). IMPLEMENTATION MAP: (1) Detection (tryBuildGatedSwitchRegion, ControlDetection.cpp) currently DECLINES distinct-base φ via the npu.1 same-base-handle check — route those to a MUX-EXCH region instead (new ControlRegion flag + per-φ base-handle→arms grouping). After substituteArm (lowerGatedSwitch step 4-pre) each φ incoming IS already the base handle (ControlledSubstitution RAUWs cq_phi→handle), so group by incoming VALUE: φ-edge→incoming block→ArmFlags[k]. (2) Lowering: replace the step-4 RAUW with: regOut=cqrt_alloc_<W>(0); for each distinct base handle q, f_q = OR of the ArmFlags of the edges selecting q (default edge → ¬OrAll, materialize via a self-inverse cqrt_x bracket like substituteArm's Negate path); emit cqrt_cswap(f_q, regOut, q); RAUW φ→regOut. Width <W> from taint.HandleWidth.lookup(base). (3) SAFETY COUPLING: npu.5 WITHOUT npu.6 is a verify-clean SILENT MISCOMPILE (non-selected sources stay entangled with the scrutinee = which-path garbage that decoheres regOut) — strictly worse than the npu.1 decline. MUST land together with npu.6; until then keep the decline. Trace runtime is structural-only (no amplitude sim), so correctness is by-construction + gate-sequence fixtures, NOT simulation-verified.
The MUX-EXCH detection gate (G0-G7) and lowering structure are specified in docs/npu6-mux-exch-gate-spec.md (npu.5+npu.6 must land atomically; npu.5 alone is a silent miscompile). The gate lives at the npu.1 decline site in tryBuildGatedSwitchRegion; the mux replaces the step-4 RAUW in lowerGatedSwitch. See the doc + [[cwk-merge-phi-discriminator]].

Detection routes distinct-base phi through G0-G7 gate (region.MuxExch). Positive fixtures _distinct (MUX-EXCH) + _distinct_3way; verify-clean. 127 LIT / 11 ctest green.

title: Phase 4.1 — gated multi-arm switch/if cascade (general side-effecting arms)
description:
Phase 4.1 follow-on (PRD §8.5, IMPL §13 WP18). The ONE multi-way shape that does NOT fold into the switch→select-chain normalization (-aht.1): a cascade of arms with ARBITRARY SIDE-EFFECTING gate bodies (distinct gate sequences / controlled arithmetic per case, not just a value or a rotation angle). There is no value to select — each arm's ops must become _controlled on its eq-flag.

Mechanism = controlled-region substitution: the Phase 4.3 WP8 symmetric two-content-arm diamond generalized to an N-way FALSE-arm chain. Compute N mutually-exclusive eq-flags (default = AND of negated flags, Toffoli ladder); control each arm's gates on its flag via LIFO cqrt_x brackets; dissolve φ via WP7's multi-φ path. This is the CQ analog of Bennett.jl's _expand_switches br-cascade — the Option-B fallback.

SEPARATE from -aht.1's select-chain unit (different mechanism — do not conflate). RED: lowering_control_switch_gated.ll (switch(q) whose arms apply distinct gate sequences to an external handle). DONE: gated multi-arm switch lowers to per-arm controlled gates; no residual switch/br i1 on a handle. Depends on u6v.1 (multi-φ dissolution) + u6v.2 (symmetric diamond).
notes:
CLARIFICATION (2026-06-02): this is an IMPLEMENTATION task, NOT a Bennett.jl import and NOT a from-scratch research spike. Bennett is a REFERENCE only — no Julia dependency. The "Option-B fallback" (br-cascade) means a CQ-side C++ desugaring modeled on Bennett's _expand_switches IDEA, reimplemented in our own LLVM pass — never linking or subprocessing Bennett. The mechanism is already chosen: generalize the Phase 4.3 WP8 symmetric two-content-arm controlled substitution to an N-way false-arm chain.

BUT the design is lighter than -aht.1's, so START WITH A DIAGNOSE-FIRST SPIKE: empirically confirm the gated-cascade shape actually survives clang -O1. We have NOT pinned the exact -O1 output the way the Phase 4.3 audit did for the 44 if-shapes; arbitrary side-effecting per-case bodies are *believed* not to fold into selects/angle-selects, but verify before implementing. Only after the shape is pinned, implement the WP8 generalization.

No urgency / no risk while open: the shape is currently SAFE — loud-diagnosed by the WP12 / u6v.6 tainted-switch guard (no silent miscompile).
close_reason: Diagnose-first spike done on real clang -O1 IR: gated cascade survives as a SwitchInst (safe). WP18 implemented — gated multi-arm switch → N-way controlled substitution (per-case eq-flags, default on ¬OR, reuse substituteArm, N-way φ dissolution, linearize). Commit ff13ead. Fixture switch_gated now POSITIVE. Spike also fixed a silent miscompile (jump-table, commit 859fc50). Follow-ons filed: 5zu (jump-table lowering), 509 (default-direct/sparse). Adjacent P1 found in review filed separately (double-φ angle).

title: Diagnose (don't silently miscompile) a tainted-arm select until the mux lands
description:

title: Mixed-arm select mux (one classical arm) via the existing HH controlled adder
description:
SHAPE: `select i1 %f, A, B` with the condition tainted and EXACTLY ONE value arm
tainted (a handle); the other arm classical (constant or runtime variable).
Real -O1 of example/test_control.c:
  %1    = icmp sgt i32 %h, -3
  %h_op = cq_template_sub_i32_lh(i32 9, i32 %h)        ; the tainted true arm (12 - a)
  %2    = select i1 %1, i32 %h_op, i32 -3              ; B = -3 is classical

CONSTRUCTION (mirrors the WP4 classical-arm reduction, PRD §2.6, with HL->HH and a
register delta). Let C be the classical arm, Q the tainted arm; ctrl = flag if Q is the
true (flag=1) arm, else the complemented flag (see below):
  1. delta = Q - C  as a REGISTER, via the existing UNCONTROLLED data template
     cq_template_sub_<W>_hl(Qhandle, Cclassical)  (no controlled form needed here).
  2. regC = cqrt_alloc_<W>(Cclassical)            (seed from the classical arm).
  3. Res  = cq_template_add_<W>_controlled(ctrl, regC, delta)   ; the HH controlled add.
     Resolver: ControlledSymbols::controlledDataTemplateFn("add", W, Shape::QQ,
     /*inverse=*/false) -> (flag, handle, handle); name = cq_template_add_<W>_controlled.
  4. RAUW the select to Res; register Res tainted + BirthOrder slot (dissolveSelect
     already does this for the classical/classical path).
Result = C + ctrl·(Q - C) = ctrl ? Q : C. For the example (Q=12-a, C=-3, ctrl=flag):
-3 + flag·((12-a)-(-3)) = flag ? (12-a) : -3. Correct.

CONTROL SENSE: if the CLASSICAL arm is the TRUE arm (select i1 %f, C, Q), seed regC and
control on the complemented flag (cqrt_x(f) bracket, uncomputed LIFO — reuse §2.5
ControlledSymbols::xFn), so result = C + ¬f·(Q-C) = f ? C : Q. (Or equivalently swap and
keep flag — pick one and pin it in the fixture.)

PASS TOUCH-POINTS (no runtime/gen_templates change):
  - ir-pass/src/ControlDetection.cpp detectControlRegions: the SelectRegion gate
    currently rejects ANY tainted arm:
       if (taint.Tainted.count(Sel->getTrueValue()) ||
           taint.Tainted.count(Sel->getFalseValue())) continue;   // line ~311
    Relax to accept EXACTLY ONE tainted arm (keep rejecting both-tainted -> that is
    child .2). Record on the ControlRegion which arm is the classical seed and the
    control sense.
  - ir-pass/src/MergeDissolution.cpp dissolveSelect: add a tainted-arm branch. Instead
    of the host Builder.CreateSub(A,B) + Shape::HL controlled add (the

title: Phase 4.1 — quantum-controlled escape (return/break/goto + measurement in shadow)
description: A tainted-branch arm that escapes the region — if(q) return...; / break / goto, or a cq_measure inside the arm — gates an escape rather than an in-place gate, so it is not a clean controlled shadow. Verified 2026-06-01: 'if (q) return a;' compiles to br + phi where one arm returns and the other measures (phi [measure(x), a]). Structural cousin of the prototype uncompute pass's ReturnInst escape check (computeFreePoint returns null on a ret user). DECISION: reject with a source-located diagnostic ('measurement/return under quantum control') vs. opt-in -fcq-measurement-bridge (backend.md §7). Acceptance: escape cases emit the chosen diagnostic (or bridge) with correct source location; negative LIT fixtures. Depends on Phase 4 core.
notes:
Audit 2026-06-02: plain 'if(q) return' and measure-in-arm DIAGNOSE cleanly today (good). BUT goto/break out of a tainted arm CRASH instead — -O1 reshapes them into multi-phi diamonds that hit Phase 4.3 Family A (u6v.1) before the escape guard fires. So this refinement now also covers goto/break, and depends on Family A landing (then they either lower or reach the escape diagnostic).
VERDICT FINALIZED 2026-06-02 (PRD §8.6, IMPL §13 WP17): REJECT-by-default is CORRECT and confirmed by the Julia stack + literature — the terminal state, not a stopgap.

- Measurement under quantum control: reject PERMANENTLY. Bennett.jl has no measure op (classical→reversible; measurement lives in Sturm/Orkan); Sturm forbids measure/return inside when(q); Silq's rejected `condMeas` IS this exact program (a measure gated on a superposed predicate is unphysical — you'd have to measure the control first).
- return/break/goto under quantum control: reject by default. Bennett cfg.jl raises a loud error on non-reconverging exits ("lower_loop!: IRRet in loop body … not supported"). Quantum Control Machine (arXiv:2304.15000) proves a superposed jump/return is non-injective and cannot be a unitary; necessary+sufficient = injectivity + synchronization (all branches reconverge). Janus Structured Reversible Program Theorem: banning arbitrary goto/break/return loses NO expressive power — refactor.

-fcq-measurement-bridge: accept ONLY as an explicit opt-in DEMOTION to classical control via deferred measurement — insert the measure AT THE REGION BOUNDARY (collapse predicate before body), loud diagnostic, and STATICALLY REJECT re-entry of the measured value into a still-coherent region (= Silq's sanctioned fix / OpenQASM-3 feed-forward). Sold as a transparent "same if" lowering it is an ANTI-PATTERN (silently changes observable behavior; Silq/Q#/Quipper refuse it).

FUTURE (capture only, not this phase): return/break via DONE-FLAG predication for the BOUNDED + RECONVERGING subset — retval register + done ancilla; write retval & set done on the exit predicate; control every post-exit op on ¬done; final return writes retval on ¬done; UNCOMPUTE done at exit (recompute predicate from live args, CNOT off) or it leaks as garbage entangled with the result. QCM/Tower/if-conversion. True non-reconverging escape stays rejected.

Sturm ships the DUAL — deferred_measurement.jl (measure-then-classical-branch → controlled gate, true=control/false=anti-control, Nielsen-Chuang §4.4) — a collapse-free optimization worth a SEPARATE future pass. The break/goto crash path is already handled by the u6v.8 catch-all diagnostic.
close_reason: WP17 — escape verdict: reject-by-default for return/measure/break/goto under quantum control, now SOURCE-LOCATED via !dbg (PRD §8.6, confirmed by Julia stack + QCM/Silq/Janus). Commit bdb7f2f. Negative fixtures: escape_measure/break/goto/dbg (+ existing escape return). The -fcq-measurement-bridge opt-in is intentionally deferred (frontend-flag + cross-region analysis; verdict flags the transparent form as an anti-pattern).

title: Phase 4.1 — tainted `switch` lowering (N-way quantum branch)
description: clang -O1 preserves a real switch instruction + N-way phi for switch(q) on a tainted scrutinee (verified 2026-06-01: 'switch i32 %q [...]' + 3-way phi survived -O1). Phase 4's select/br normalization does not cover it. Options: (a) DEFAULT — pre-run stock LLVM -lowerswitch before cq-lowering, folding the switch into icmp-eq chains + selects/brs so it collapses into shapes Phase 4 already handles; (b) native multi-way controlled mux (control on q==0, q==1, ...). Acceptance: a switch(q) program lowers to the expected controlled trace; LIT fixture pins the chosen normalization. Depends on Phase 4 core.
notes:
Audit 2026-06-02 (PRD §7 Family E): the 'pre-run stock -lowerswitch' default is NOT free. -lowerswitch emits a balanced pivot TREE (icmp slt/eq + br with SHARED MULTI-PRED phi-merges); matchDiamond accepts a shared multi-pred merge -> linearization frees a still-referenced block -> CRASH. Surviving switch (no lowerswitch) silently miscompiles (branches on quantum handle id) — now guarded by Phase 4.3 Family D diagnostic (u6v.6). Switch lowering here depends on Phase 4.3 A (u6v.1) + C (u6v.2) landing first AND a NEW closed-diamond guard in matchDiamond (require merge has exactly 2 preds = Pred,Arm); then re-verify the pivot-tree path.
DIRECTION FINALIZED 2026-06-02 (PRD §8.2, IMPL §13 WP15): switch lowering = data-flow SELECT-CHAIN normalization, NOT -lowerswitch. A `normalizeTaintedSwitch` step (between taint-prop and region detection) rewrites a tainted-scrutinee SwitchInst + N-way merge φ into `icmp eq` flags + a nested `select` chain, then the EXISTING dissolveSelect/reduceClassicalMux path lowers it (icmp-eq HL flags + classical-mux/mux.1 controlled adds).

Supersedes Family E ("-lowerswitch + closed-diamond guard"): the select form never produces br-diamonds, so it sidesteps the pivot-tree shared-multi-pred-merge CRASH this issue's own notes found, AND needs no N-way φ dissolution (φ collapses to binary selects) and no new ABI.

Confirmed against Bennett.jl `_expand_switches` (fetched+verified 2026-06-02): same "eliminate switch by reduction" move, but Bennett targets a br-cascade because its downstream is gate-emission-over-CFG; CQ targets selects because downstream is opcode-replacement-over-dataflow. CQ also never inherits Bennett's U11 global-φ-incoming-rewrite trap (we read then DELETE the φ; merge becomes single-pred).

Scope: first cut = value-merge, break-terminated, clean reconverge (merge preds = case/default only). Also covers multi-way value `if` for FREE (PRD §8.3) and angle-switch via angle-select-chain (NEW WP16, generalizes u6v.4/WP10). Gated SIDE-EFFECTING multi-arm cascade is split to a NEW follow-on (different mechanism: controlled substitution / Bennett br-cascade fallback). Gate-level depth opt (unary iteration / QROM, arXiv:1805.03662) is BELOW the cqrt_* ABI = runtime concern, not this issue. Depends: u6v.1 (multi-φ infra) + u6v.4 (angle-select).

title: Phase 7: lower cq_invert_* brackets to adjoint sequences
description: Manual inversion (cq_invert_begin/_end) is unimplemented in the cq-lowering pass (no invert/_inv refs in ir-pass/src). Semantics (frontend.md 3.5, backend.md 10): the bracketed region lowers to the ADJOINT of its gate sequence — reverse order, each op inverted (rotations negate angle; NOT/CNOT/Toffoli self-adjoint; arithmetic uses the runtime *_inv templates, which already ship). Today the __cq_invert_begin/_end markers survive lowering as calls (won't link) and the bracketed op lowers to the plain forward template.

title: ir-pass: canonicalize Q+Q operand order by handle creation time
description: clang -O1 canonicalizes commutative add operands by SSA index, so the runtime trace for 'quantum int c = a + b;' depends on which handle was alloc'd first by clang's IR-numbering — currently worked_example traces (h1, h0) and full_example's Q+Q add traces (h4, h3). A future clang version could change this; the e2e harness uses byte-exact diff so we'd get spurious failures. Fix: in step 5 of CQLoweringPass.cpp, track handle creation order via a DenseMap<Value*, unsigned> BirthOrder (Allocs assigned in step 2, cq_template_add_i32 results assigned in step 5). When lowering a Q+Q add (both operands in Tainted), order the call's operands by BirthOrder so the older handle becomes lhs. This restores PLAN.md §4.7.1's canonical (h0, h1) format and makes the trace stable across clang versions. Refresh worked_example and full_example expected.log after landing.

title: Phase 4 prototype: validate region handling (cq_when_*) on stock LLVM
description: Add a fourth pass cq-control that, within cq_when_begin/cq_when_end brackets, substitutes each cqrt_template_* call with its _controlled variant (taking the region's control handle as an additional first argument). Validates that region detection + controlled-variant substitution is implementable on stock LLVM, which is the one architectural mechanism (region handling) the existing Phase 2/5/7 prototypes have not touched.
design: cq-control operates on post-lowering IR (after cq-lowering has dissolved qint_mid_t and emitted cqrt_*). For prototype simplicity, the test input declares cq_when_begin as taking i32 directly (the handle), avoiding the qint_mid_t→handle resolution that real integration would need. Linear CFG only — begin and end in same BB. No nested regions. The mechanism: walk each BB, track 'current control' state, for each cqrt_template_* call inside a region emit a _controlled variant with the control prepended to args, erase brackets at end.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds against stock LLVM 19 (additions only — existing passes unaffected). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-control runs without crash on hand-written post-lowering input. 3. Output passes opt -verify. 4. cq_when_begin and cq_when_end call sites erased. 5. cqrt_template_add_i32 inside the region is replaced by cqrt_template_add_i32_controlled with the control handle as the first argument. 6. cqrt_template_* calls OUTSIDE any region are NOT substituted (verified by adding a second template call after cq_when_end).
notes: Out of scope for this validation increment: qint_mid_t→handle resolution at cq_when_begin (would be an extension to cq-lowering); cross-BB regions (real cq_when_* can span branches); nested regions (multi-control accumulation); the inverse case cq_invert_begin/_end (separate but similar mechanism reusing emit_inverse from Phase 5). Companion: docs/architecture.md §5.1 + §7.5 (region brackets), docs/backend.md §5.9 (region handling spec).
close_reason: Phase 4 region-handling prototype succeeds. New cq-control pass (~80 LOC) walks each BB tracking cq_when_begin/end bracket state; for each cqrt_template_* call inside a region, substitutes the _controlled variant prepending the control handle. Test verifies: inside-region call replaced, outside-region call preserved, brackets erased, exactly 1 controlled call site + 1 plain call site. title: Phase 7 prototype: validate call-graph specialization on stock LLVM
description: Extend the prototype/ pass plugin with a third pass cq-specialize that demonstrates function cloning + call-site retargeting via stock LLVM CloneFunction / CloneFunctionInto + ValueToValueMapTy. For each call site with a qint_mid_t-typed argument, clone the callee, rename to __cq_q_<f>_q1, and retarget the call site. design: Use CloneFunction(F, VMap) to clone the callee preserving signature. Set linkage to private/internal so DCE can remove the original if all uses are retargeted. Rename via Function::setName. Walk call sites of the original; for each whose arg is qint_mid_t-typed, replace setCalledFunction to the clone. Minimal scope: signature is preserved, no Bennett wrap-around (forward + CNOT-copy + reverse) — that is downstream implementation that uses the same already-validated emit_inverse mechanism from Phase 5. The point here is to confirm CloneFunction + call-site retargeting compose with the existing cq-lowering pass.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds against stock LLVM 19 (no patches). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-specialize runs without crash on a test input with one function-call site. 3. Output IR passes opt -verify. 4. A new function named __cq_q_<original>_q1 exists in the module. 5. The clone has the same signature as the original (signature rewriting deferred). 6. The original call site is replaced with a call to the clone. 7. Both functions (original + clone) are well-formed.
notes: Out of scope: signature rewriting to (i32, i32) handle ABI, Bennett wrap-around (forward + CNOT-copy + reverse), specialization caching across multiple call sites, recursion handling, q-arg-mask discrimination beyond binary 'has qint_mid_t arg or not'. These are downstream once cloning + retargeting compose with lowering. Companion: bd memory prototype-validated-no-fork-2026-05-22, docs/llvm-fork-analysis.md §8.2.
close_reason: Phase 7 prototype validates call-graph specialization. cq-specialize pass uses stock LLVM CloneFunction (+ ValueToValueMapTy) to clone callees with qint_mid_t-typed args, renames via __cq_q_<f>_q1 mangling, retargets call sites. Test: opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-specialize produces a clone with internal linkage that preserves the original function's body shape (extractvalue + add + insertvalue + ret), call site in @example now references the clone, zero remaining calls to the original from @example, output passes opt -verify. design: Use FunctionAnalysisManagerModuleProxy to obtain PostDominatorTreeAnalysis from a Module pass. Output IR passes opt -verify. 4. Each handle (cqrt_alloc_classical_i32 result, cqrt_alloc_i32 result) has a cqrt_free(handle) call emitted after its last use. 5. title: Candidate->control cascade: a Phase-6 spec candidate whose RESULT feeds an onward tainted-condition control region
description:
Physics-valid remaining safe over-decline in the dugh Phase-4x6 arc (the sibling of 9paa/afmv, which handle a spec candidate READING a merge/control rail). Here the candidate's RESULT is the quantum value that feeds further control.

SHAPE: a control-merge %out feeds a Phase-6 spec candidate g(%out) (round-1 Pending or round-2 new), and g's RESULT %z = call @g(%out) then feeds a DOWNSTREAM tainted-condition control region: if(%z>k){...} / switch(%z){...} / %z>k ? a : b.

CURRENT BEHAVIOR / ORDERING TENSION: in repropagateControlMerges, %out re-taints so %z (the call result) taints, then detectAndLowerOnwardControl (yn71) sees the tainted-condition region on %z. But g is NOT cloned/Bennett-wrapped until the step-262 driver (specialize), which runs AFTER repropagateControlMerges. So the downstream control region is adjudicated while %z is still  — a not-yet-reversible user-function-call result, not a lowered cqrt_* handle. The region either lowers routing on that raw %z (fragile) or loud-declines. The spec re-plan/re-detect (replanReseedSpecialization / detectSpecializations) only update plan6.Pending; they do not emit the clone, so the clone's ReturnTainted/handle identity is unknown at control-lowering time.

description:

IMPORTANT nuance (verified 2026-07-01): the blocked *l rows fail TODAY at a _Generic COMPILE error ('controlling expression type long double not compatible with any generic association type'), because include/CQ.h has NO long double association at all -- NOT because backend f80 math is missing. So the blocker is layered: (1) frontend _Generic gap (always needed); (2) backend f80 width (needed only where long double==x86_fp80/fp128). Host check 2026-07-01: this machine is x86_64, long double==x86_fp80 (16B), so BOTH layers are needed here.
design:
Concrete work surface (verified 2026-07-01):
1. include/CQ.h -- _Generic STOPS at f64/f16 (no long double). Add long double -> cq_theta_f80 / cq_phi_f80 / cq_measure_f80 (per-target symbol; see platform policy).
2. ir-pass/src/OpcodeSupport.cpp -- abiWidthFromType: add ty->isX86_FP80Ty()->'f80' and ty->isFP128Ty()->'f128' (today only isHalfTy/isFloatTy/isDoubleTy). fpBits: f80=80, f128=128.
3. ir-pass/src/WidthDispatch.cpp -- suffix->width table (~:37), typeForWidth (Type::getX86_FP80Ty/getFP128Ty), and the dead-decl symbol sweep list (~:468: cq_theta_f80/cq_phi_f80/cq_measure_f80).
4. runtime: tools/opcode_table.yaml + tools/libm_table.yaml add f80/f128 width rows; regenerate via tools/gen_templates.py; SHA-256 drift check (gen_templates.py --check) gates it. Add cqrt_alloc_f80/ry_f80/rz_f80/measure_f80 to the hand-written core ABI (runtime/cq_runtime.{h,c}).
5. Angle fence ALREADY generalizes to >64-bit (WidthDispatch.cpp:139) -- f80/f128 as a rotation angle already declines; NO new angle hazard.

PLATFORM POLICY (decide up front): long double is x86_fp80 on x86-64 (this host; datalayout f80:128), fp128 on AArch64 Linux, and f64 (==double) on Apple Silicon / MSVC. The _Generic maps the C long double token to ONE runtime symbol, so the seed width must track the TARGET ABI. On long-double==double targets, ONLY step 1 is needed (maps to cq_theta_f64, zero backend change). v1 recommendation: support x86_fp80 (f80) for this host; carry f128 as a parallel width for AArch64.
acceptance_criteria: abiWidthFromType recognizes x86_fp80->f80 (and fp128->f128); tainted *l math.h variants lower instead of declining 'unsupported width'. CQ.h _Generic seeds long double. Positive lit fixture(s) for a long double slice (tainted long double add + a libm *l e.g. sqrtl) + >=1 e2e golden smoke. NEGATIVE preserved: a long double value as a rotation angle STILL declines (angle fence). gen_templates.py --check drift passes; runtime archives build. Coverage regenerated (probe.py run) -- the *l bucket flips blocked->verified. Rule-13 cleared (width-only but touches FROZEN ABI surfaces + the frontend seed).

description: Surfaced while verifying fch8 (a false alarm — see bd memory fch8-inloop-control-false-alarm). title: InvokeInst-borne cq_theta/cq_measure never seeded as taint source/sink (dyn_cast<CallInst> gap)
description: PRE-EXISTING (found during the test_C_libtooling-udw §adversarial review, 2026-06-11, under-decline lens; UNRELATED to udw). TaintPropagation.cpp collectAndSeed() and isMeasureSink() use dyn_cast<CallInst>, which returns null on an InvokeInst. So a cq_theta_<sfx> reached via 'invoke' is never added to ThetaCalls and never seeded into Tainted (its result is treated CLASSICAL); a cq_measure_<sfx> via 'invoke' is never recognized as a sink. Consequences: an invoke'd theta never lowers (survives as an undefined @cq_theta extern -> Stage-3 LINK error, loud-ish) and its result, used downstream, propagates no taint. Plain C + clang -O1 with NO exceptions emits 'call', not 'invoke', so this is not reachable from the supported frontend today (hence P3) — but the pass should be robust: either handle CallBase uniformly or loudly decline an invoke of a front-end intrinsic. NOTE the taint-escape guard already uses dyn_cast<CallBase> (catches invokes of UNKNOWN callees), so the gap is specifically the SOURCE/SINK seeding, not the escape side. Fix: switch collectAndSeed/isMeasureSink to CallBase, or add an explicit 'front-end intrinsic via invoke' decline. Add a decline (or accept) fixture.

title: Swap-route design: mint the control flag at the COMPARE's program point (lift the 'condition predates a non-diagonal gate' conservative decline)
description: The 9hh §8 clearance found (and conservatively declined) the chained-Ry stale-condition shape: c = (q>5); q = cq_theta(q, t2); if (c) {...}. title: Both-arms-handle select mux (alloc-zero + two controlled adds; preserve reused arms)
description:
SHAPE: `select i1 %f, %hp, %hq` — condition tainted and BOTH value arms tainted handles.
The mixed-arm reduction (.1) cannot apply: cqrt_alloc seeds from a CLASSICAL value, and
here neither arm is classical.

CONSTRUCTION (still NO cswap/Fredkin needed — that is only an in-place alternative):
  1. regOut = cqrt_alloc_<W>(0).
  2. cq_template_add_<W>_controlled(f,  regOut, hp)     ; regOut += f·hp
  3. cqrt_x(f)                                          ; form ¬f (LIFO-bracketed)
     cq_template_add_<W>_controlled(f, regOut, hq)      ; regOut += ¬f·hq
     cqrt_x(f)                                          ; restore f
  Result = f·hp + ¬f·hq = f ? hp : hq.
Both hp and hq are READ (a_handle/b_handle operands), never consumed -> PRESERVED for
their other uses. This is the load-bearing difference from .1: an arm here may be live
elsewhere in the function, so a consuming/in-place strategy is unsafe; the additive
copy into a fresh ancilla preserves them.

PASS TOUCH-POINTS: extend the .1 detection gate to ALSO accept both-tainted; add the
both-tainted branch in dissolveSelect emitting alloc(0) + the two controlled adds + the
¬f cqrt_x bracket (reuse ControlledSymbols::xFn and the §2.5 De Morgan LIFO uncompute
discipline). Depends on .1 (shares the detection + dissolution seam).

UNCOMPUTE: regOut is the result (kept); the ¬f X-bracket is uncomputed in place; hp/hq
and any inputs are data temporaries left for Phase 5. Phase 4 brackets the control flag
+ the ¬f X-bracket only.

PRIORITY: lower than .1 — rarer shape (both branch values quantum); .1 covers the
common case. RED fixture: lowering_control_mux_handles_i32.ll; e2e slice modeled on
e2e-slice-control-merge.

NOTE: if a future need wants in-place routing instead of additive copy, cqrt_cswap /
Fredkin (+ controlled/inverse) is the alternative primitive — but it is NOT required to
land this issue.
acceptance_criteria: A 'y=(q>0)?f(q):g(q)' program lowers to cqrt_alloc(0) + two cq_template_add_*_controlled with an uncomputed ¬f cqrt_x bracket; both source handles still referenced afterward; LIT + e2e green; opt -verify clean.
close_reason: Both-arms-handle select mux implemented (gate accepts both-tainted; dissolveSelect alloc(0)+two QQ controlled adds+¬f cqrt_x bracket; arms preserved). LIT+e2e green; opt -verify clean; WP3-WP6 + mux.1 byte-identical. Reviewer ACCEPT.

title: Build -O-level regression matrix for stage-1 clang flag
description: Build a regression test matrix that lets the stage-1 clang -O level be raised above the validated -O1 floor with confidence. Per docs/frontend.md §8 'Optimization-level guidance', stage 1 is currently pinned at -O1 because higher levels introduce risks (aggressive inline pre-empting clone-on-taint; IPSCCP/argpromotion rewriting signatures; LoopUnroll/LoopVectorize on tainted loops; SimplifyCFG flattening branches the post-dom walk depends on; GVN CSE across tainted values; SLPVectorize fusing tainted+untainted scalars into a vector op at -O3). Matrix: small CQ programs compiled at -O0/-O1/-O2/-O3 (each), lowered IR diffed across levels, runtime gate sequences captured and compared. Goal: identify which risks fire in practice, which are theoretical, and whether the stage-1 default can move from -O1 to -O2/-O3 unconditionally or with specific -fno-* flags. Related: 5kb.
notes:
Re-deferred 2026-05-29 (pending Phase 3). Original deferral blockers ARE cleared: CQ.h has cq_theta/phi/measure; ir-pass targets @cq_theta_*; tests/e2e is a working end-to-end compile route. Probed the floor anyway — ran the full pipeline (clang -O$N -emit-llvm | opt cq-lowering | clang link | run) at -O0..-O3 on 6 probes (straightline/inline/loop/dup/slp/branch).

FINDINGS: -O0 correctly REJECTED by the pass (no mem2reg => taint stuck in allocas; floor confirmed from below). -O1==-O2==-O3 BYTE-IDENTICAL gate traces for all 6 probes — none of the frontend.md §8 risks fires. BUT the Phase-2 surface is too narrow to be a real test: only add/fadd lower, and 'if(flag){x=x+1}' collapses to an unconditional 'add; select i1' at -O1 *before the pass runs* (verified in IR), so there is no O1->O2 delta to catch. Real risks needing a verdict (SLPVectorize — clang declined to vectorize 2 i32 adds feeding opaque calls; LoopVectorize; IPSCCP/argpromotion signature rewrite; non-flattening guarded blocks) require the Phase-3 opcode surface (icmp/sub/mul/casts) + richer control flow. A green matrix today would over-claim.

RESUME when Phase 3 opcode lowering lands: build tests/omatrix/ then. Verified findings + corrected baseline in bd memory 'omatrix-baseline-macos'. (A prior in-session 'SimplifyCFG hazard fires' claim was WRONG — based on unread report files — now corrected; it does not fire on this surface.)

title: Investigate -O2/-O3 viability at stage 1 (post-rest)
description: Currently the pipeline pins clang -O1 at stage 1 (pre-IR-pass). -O1 is the validated floor — minimum needed for mem2reg/SROA cleanup. Higher levels are not prohibited by the design but introduce risks that need a test matrix. Defer until the rest of the taint-driven pipeline transition (frontend.md/backend.md/quantum-classical-handling.md/example.md/ROADMAP) is done.
notes: Stage 1 risks at -O2+: aggressive inline pre-empts clone-on-taint; IPSCCP/argpromotion can rewrite signatures; LoopUnroll/LoopVectorize on tainted loops/conditions; SimplifyCFG flattens branches the post-dom analysis walks; GVN CSE across tainted values. Stage 1 risks at -O3: SLPVectorize can fuse tainted + untainted scalar ops into a single vector op — would silently miscompile without vector-tainted-op template support. Stage 3 (post-pass codegen): any -O level safe — only stock LLVM ops + opaque cqrt_* externals remain; this is where most binary runtime perf comes from anyway. Recommendation: default -O1 stage 1, allow -O3 stage 3, require -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize if user pushes -O3 to stage 1 until vector-tainted templates exist. Need: regression test matrix (small CQ programs compiled at each -O level, lowered IR diffed, runtime gate sequences compared).

title: diagnoseMalformedDecl uses dyn_cast<CallInst> — invoke-only malformed reserved-name decl loses !dbg source location
description: PRE-EXISTING, ORTHOGONAL follow-up surfaced during the test_C_libtooling-rzs9 §adversarial review (completeness lens, 2026-06-11). TaintPropagation.cpp diagnoseMalformedDecl() walks F->users() with dyn_cast<CallInst> to pick the first call site for the DiagnosticInfoUnsupported function-context + !dbg. A malformed-prototype reserved-name decl (cq_theta_/cq_phi_/cq_measure_ with the wrong FunctionType) reached ONLY via 'invoke' (no plain-call users) finds no CallInst user and falls to the decl-level diagnostic (the F-context overload, no instruction !dbg) — STILL LOUD (opt exits non-zero), just without source-line precision. NOT a soundness issue: the precondition is a WRONG PROTOTYPE (orthogonal to rzs9's wrong CALL-FORM), a malformed decl never enters the FnSets, and clang -O1 on exception-free C never emits 'invoke' for opaque externs (doubly unreachable). Fix: switch the user scan to dyn_cast<CallBase> so an invoke'd call site supplies the !dbg, same generalization rzs9 applied to collectAndSeed/isMeasureSink. Diagnostic-precision hardening only — low priority. Add a fixture if fixed.

Same generalization rzs9 applied to collectAndSeed/isMeasureSink. Regression fixture lowering_reject_decl_prototype_invoke.ll (red-greens via mal.c:7:9 CHECK). Phase 5 WI-4 emission soundness (Uncomputation.cpp emitDagReversal + the Placeable check). (A) PER-RAIL FREE: free each rail right after the adjoint of its EARLIEST-program-order creating gate -- for a cq_template producer that is the producer (its result IS the rail); for an alloc-root handle it is the FIRST rotation (a handle with N rotations, e.g. theta then cq_phi, frees ONCE after the earliest rotation's adjoint). Implemented as DenseMap<rail,earliest-gate> built by iterating D.Calls in FORWARD order (first-occurrence wins); emit walks D.Calls in REVERSE and frees rail R iff Earliest[R]==G. Because the earliest gate is emitted LAST among its rail's reverse-touches, the free lands after every reverse-read => no UAF; and one map value per key => double-free is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE. (B) REVERSE-PROGRAM-ORDER == REVERSE-TOPOLOGICAL-ORDER is sound ONLY because the driver's Placeable check requires every gate to DOMINATE the single insertion point At (dagInsertPoint = common post-dom of all Insert terminals' FreePoint.At, after the latest); dominators of a node form a CHAIN, so gates that all dominate At are TOTALLY ordered by dominance => reverse program order is an unambiguous reverse-topo order. A gate that does NOT dominate At (sibling-block / multi-component-in-exclusive-arms) fails Placeable => whole DAG safe-leaked, never emitted misordered. (C) WI-4 now ALSO frees intermediate template-result rails (WI-3 leaked them); existing linear fixtures (chain_reassign/cast_chain/lh_slot/dead_sibling_no_measure) stayed GREEN WITHOUT regeneration because their ordered CHECK sequences have no CHECK-NOT on free, so added intermediate frees are tolerated.

Phase 6 STALE-CLASSICAL-ATTR hazard (latent since 6.1, surfaced by the 6.3 void twin; fix in SpecializeClone.cpp stripStaleClassicalAttrs, called by cloneFor AND synthUncomputeTwin). A specialization clone is CloneFunction-d from a PURE-CLASSICAL body, inheriting its fn/return/param attributes -- which the quantum-lowered body INVALIDATES: it now calls side-effecting trace primitives (cqrt_*/cq_template_* print, cqrt_free deallocs) and returns a fresh i32 handle. TWO failure modes, both caught by Rule-13 adversarial review, NEITHER by the green suite: (1) SILENT-MISCOMPILE -- memory(none)+willreturn+nounwind on the clone let the backend DELETE a void clone call whose result is unused (the 6.3 uncompute twin call) even at the e2e -O0 link, leaving the entangled inner rail freed DIRTY (hidden measurement, collapses the borrowed qubit). The forward clone dodged it (result always used); the void twin is the first unused-result clone call. (2) CRASH (opt -verify exit 134) -- the twin RETYPES the return to void but CloneFunctionInto copies the forward clone i32-only return attrs (noundef/signext/zeroext/range); noundef or range on a VOID return is malformed. Triggers on ANY inner whose clang -O1 return carries noundef (non-full-range op: a AND 255, a XOR 3, a SHR 2, identity); the a*7 golden DODGED it by luck (full overflow range so no return attr). FIX (stripStaleClassicalAttrs, single chokepoint, Rule 14): setMemoryEffects(unknown); removeFnAttr WillReturn+NoFree; if return is VOID clear the ENTIRE ReturnIndex attr set, else removeRetAttr(Range); removeParamAttr Returned on all args (a clone returns a fresh copy-out, never the borrowed param, so a Returned param attr would let the optimizer substitute the borrowed handle for the basis copy). Verified: opt exit 0, verify clean, and the -O2 relink keeps every twin+free call (no DCE). REGRESSION PIN: spec_accept_transitive_retattr.ll (inner ret has explicit noundef range). LESSON: clone-then-repurpose ALWAYS audit inherited attributes -- they encode assumptions the new body breaks; removing attrs is always correctness-safe (only drops opt licenses). See [[6-3-transitive-done]].

Phase 7.1 Increment D BLOCKER discovered 2026-06-20 (empirical, clang 19.1.7, x86_64-apple-darwin AND x86_64-linux): the IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN-7.1 §6 i128 mechanism is FALSE on this toolchain. A C __int128 / unsigned __int128 function parameter+return is DECOMPOSED by the C ABI into {i64,i64} aggregates: cq_theta_si128(__int128,double)->__int128 emits as '{i64,i64} @cq_theta_si128(i64,i64,double)', NOT 'i128 @cq_theta_si128(i128,double)'. So abiWidthFromType (expects 128-bit IntegerType) and declMatchesPrototype (expects i128 source) NEVER recognize the source; the taint seed would be a {i64,i64} aggregate. Worse, a tainted 'add i128' on a small constant is SPLIT by clang into add-i128-on-low-half + separate add-i64-on-high-half threaded by extractvalue/zext/trunc/lshr, and the sink cq_measure_si128 takes 2 i64 args. Even i128-as-INTERMEDIATE is fragile: -O1 demanded-bits ELIMINATES the i128 entirely ((i128)q*(i128)q truncated to i64 folds to 'mul i64'). CONTRAST: f16 is PERFECTLY CLEAN end-to-end -- 'half @cq_theta_f16(half,double)', 'fadd half', 'half @cq_measure_f16(half)' -- f16 ships exactly as the plan describes. CONSEQUENCE: i128 cannot be a frozen frontend source/sink as IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN-7.1 D6 assumed; doing it needs aggregate-taint seeding + i128/i64 split-op coalescing + 2-arg measure (a real sub-project, NOT Increment-D-sized). Recommendation: ship f16 in Increment D, defer i128 to a tracked pre-freeze follow-up exactly like R-D did for _BitInt. RULE 11 vindicated: the plan GUESSED __int128->i128; verification disproved it BEFORE any frozen symbol was minted.

Phase 7.4 break — CAPTURE RESOURCE refinement (owner question 2026-06-25: 'two new flags per iteration?'). The earlier 7.4-break-design-crux sketch used a cqrt_cswap MOVE-capture + done-flag; that is O(K) ancilla, NOT O(1): a move zeroes the fired-branch rail so the break flag brk=cond(rail) can't be recomputed -> can't uncompute in-iteration; and the latch scratch fire=brk AND NOT done records WHICH iteration first fired (which-path), un-recoverable from (brk,done) alone -> both accumulate to O(K), needing a trip-sized scratch array (gives up dynamic-K). CORRECTED O(1) mechanism (PRD-7.4 §2.2/§2.2a): (1) COPY-NOT-MOVE capture cqrt_copy_<W>_controlled(fire, rail, R) — basis-value CNOT-copy, Rule-8-legal, rail left INTACT so brk recomputes -> uncompute in-iteration; (2) a FIRST-BREAK INDEX register idx (iN = loop-counter width; idx==0 ≡ not-yet-fired; on first fire idx<-i+1, +1 so iter 0 ≠ not-fired) subsumes the done-flag AND records WHERE, so fire is recomputable in-iteration as (idx==i+1) -> uncompute in-iteration. Per-iter scratch (brk, fire, idx==0 eq-flag) all return to |0> before the backedge -> forward body is a CLEAN per-iteration unitary on (rail,R,idx) only. Carried state crossing the backedge = rail + R + idx = O(1), independent of K, dynamic-K preserved. Exit consolidation cqrt_copy_<W>_controlled(idx==0, rail, R) gives never-broke branches the full-trip value. Then copy R->out, then whole-loop reverse-play (backward companion loop, emitInverseChain, n times) cleans R/idx/rail and disentangles out. Rule-13 hazards: scratch must be uncomputed in-iteration (else O(K)/dirty carry); idx==0 gate must make capture idempotent (no re-capture); reverse-play must replay exactly n times. ABI all existing: cqrt_copy_<W>_controlled (involution, no _inv twin, runtime cq_runtime.h:282-286), cqrt_toffoli, cqrt_x/cnot, cqrt_alloc_iN. NO cqrt_cswap in the capture path now. Phase 7.4 controlled break (epic y05j) — CORRECTED design crux + owner decision 2026-06-25. EARLIER WRONG FRAMING (do not repeat): a rolled-loop break over a per-iteration gate was claimed 'fundamentally unsound — needs unroll+_controlled-rotation or a cross-iteration done-flag carrying un-uncomputable which-path info → Rule-5 measurement / no-cloning'. ABORT/EXIT UNDER QUANTUM CONTROL = PARK CASCADE, not gate-the-tape (owner discussion 2026-06-19; design direction). A noreturn sink (@abort/@exit/__assert_fail/llvm.trap; -O1 shape: tainted-cond br -> arm with 'tail call void @abort()' + unreachable, NO merge phi -> non-reconverging) in a tainted-condition arm joins the Phase-7.2/7.4 EXIT-PRIORITY PARK CASCADE (same primitive as controlled return/break): mint abort-flag, cswap live regs into a graveyard under the flag (pre-abort state preserved + inspectable), let downstream run UNCONTROLLED, record the flag -> TRUNCATE the output tape at the abort point at inspection. WHY park is both correct AND cheap for abort specifically: abort TERMINATES -> there is NO coherent downstream -> the branch-correlated tail-garbage on the working rails is NEVER observed and never dephases (harmless, same cost already accepted from swap-route arms). Do NOT gate every downstream op on not-flag (drastically too costly AND pointless). GATE-THE-TAPE (controlled cqrt_copy) is reserved ONLY for the NON-terminating conditional-output case (Tier 0, keep computing coherently). Abort = the NON-RECONVERGING, NO-VALUE-SELECT member of the cascade family; return/break PRESERVE+SELECT a value so they carry the 7.2 tail-garbage core-hazard, which abort sidesteps. TAINT-DRIVEN PIPELINE — design landed on branch taint-driven-pipeline (rewrite from prior AST-frontend design). Live docs: docs/{frontend,backend,quantum-classical-handling,llvm-implementation,example}.md + docs/rationale/proposal-taint-driven-pipeline.md. Prior AST-frontend design archived at docs/archive/old-design/.

KEY DECISIONS:
(1) Frontend = CQ.h header + stock Clang -O1 -emit-llvm -include CQ.h. NO rewriter, NO custom parser, NO quantum keyword, NO special types. transpiler/ + tools/cqc are archived.
(2) Intrinsic surface = 4 families ONLY: cq_theta (Ry, SOLE taint source), cq_phi (Rz, propagates only, deleted on classical operand), cq_measure (sole sink, return is classical), cq_invert_begin/_end (manual inversion bracket). 14 standard C scalar types × _Generic dispatch in CQ.h.
(3) RETIRED — do NOT propose: cq_init_*, cq_alloc_* (as user surface), cq_when_begin/_end, quantum keyword/macro, qint_mid_t / q*_mid_t struct types, arithmetic intrinsics like cq_add_qq / cq_mul_qc, measurement-as-cast.
(4) Allocation is GATE-TRIGGERED: cqrt_alloc_<W> inserted at first cq_theta whose operand is still classical. Variables declared but never rotated produce no qubits.
(5) Taint is a property of SSA values, not declarations. Forward propagation from @cq_theta returns drives: allocation insertion, opcode lowering (mixed Q+C via _hl variants), controlled-form lowering, call-graph specialization, per-op uncomputation.
(6) Controlled regions recovered STRUCTURALLY from tainted br i1 via PostDominatorTree. No source-level cq_when_* marker.
(7) Per-op compile-time adjoints emitted at SSA last-use via PostDominatorTree::findNearestCommonDominator. Whole-call Bennett used only at one boundary: clone-synthesis (backend.md §7.2, §9.4) — never for uncomputation.
(8) Backend ships forward + controlled-forward templates only. Adjoint and controlled-adjoint derived via emit_inverse (reverse + per-gate adjoint).
(9) Two function-lifting paths: curated symbol substitution (opaque externals — libm, LLVM intrinsics) + clone-on-taint (LTO-visible bodies, keyed by tainted-arg signature mask). Original classical fn preserved alongside specialization.
(10) Runtime ABI is width-only (cqrt_alloc_i32 covers signed + unsigned). Signedness lives in the LLVM opcode (add nsw vs nuw, icmp slt vs ult); frontend intrinsics carry signedness suffix for source clarity; IR pass strips it when lowering.
(11) NO LLVM fork, NO MLIR dialect for v1. Validated 2026-05-22 by prototype/ against stock LLVM 19.1.7. MLIR re-evaluation deferred to Phase 10 freeze gate (ROADMAP §9).
(12) Phase numbering 0-10 in ROADMAP.md. Old v1-era roadmap at docs/archive/old-design/ROADMAP.md — note any 'Phase N' reference in older memories may refer to OLD numbering, not new.

cqrt_copy_<W> (Phase 4.2, the design's ONLY new ABI; PRD Part II §8.1) — the keep-sources-live reversible basis copy |x>_src|0>_dst -> |x>_src|x>_dst, one transversal CNOT per bit. INVARIANTS (binding): (a) 5 INTEGER WIDTHS ONLY — cqrt_copy_i{1,8,16,32,64}; there is deliberately NO cqrt_copy_f32/_f64 because an FP merge phi under tainted control is categorically an ANGLE not data (the f64 silent-miscompile family) — the pass can never legitimately mint an FP copy, so an FP copy symbol's only possible caller is exactly that bug. Width at emit is read from the chain op's integer SSA type via abiWidthFromType (pre-RAUW the chain ops still carry iN), NOT the cq_theta suffix. (b) INVOLUTION, NO _inv TWIN — applying it twice returns dst to |0> (same class as cqrt_x/cqrt_cswap); EmitInverse must never emit a cqrt_copy adjoint. (c) NEVER FREES/CONSUMES/DISENTANGLES ITS SOURCE (Rule 8) — it copies a basis LABEL, not a state; freeing a superposed source stays cqrt_cswap-only (move, not copy). The routed value register is left allocated after the copy (restored to p0 by reverse-play, stays entangled with out as program data; freeing it would be a hidden measurement, Rule 6). (d) WRONG FOR ANY PHASE/SUPERPOSITION CARRIER (Rule 7) — a CNOT copy of an Rz/Ry answer dephases it (verified P0 0.585->0.500); method-B and cqrt_copy are VALUE-ARM ONLY, every phase fixture keeps CHECK-NOT cqrt_copy. (e) HAND-WRITTEN cqrt_* CORE (runtime/cq_runtime.{h,c}, the cqrt_cswap precedent), NOT the generated YAML surface — gen_templates.py --check stays clean because opcode_table.yaml is untouched. The Phase-8/10 ABI freeze re-opened for exactly these 5 symbols. Minted lazily via WidthDispatch::copyFn. Trace: 'cqrt_copy_<W>(h<src>, h<dst>)' (no-arrow void, like cqrt_cswap).

NAMED INVARIANT (Phase 4.2 WI-7, IMPLEMENTATION-4.2 §6.2): cqrt_copy MUST keep counting as a FORWARD CONSUMER in ChainWalk (forwardConsumerCount/HasFanOut, ChainWalk.cpp:73,138). WHY: in the value-arm method-B stream the per-op uncompute pass runs LAST and must add NO free for the region (net frees = exactly 2 diamond / 3 if/else; out and the restored source p are never freed — either is a hidden measurement). Two guards combine: (a) 'out' is held out of the uncompute net by isTerminalHandle (its only non-benign user is the measure sink / ret escape). (b) The routed SOURCE register p is held out by HasFanOut: cqrt_copy(p,out) is a CallInst user of p that is neither an in-place gate on p nor a measure sink, so forwardConsumerCount counts it as a forward consumer -> p has fan-out (the route cswaps AND the copy) -> recoverForwardChain bails rather than walking a chain through p (which could otherwise reach a spurious free of p, or of a dead chain rooted at out). HAZARD: a future refinement of the fan-out exemption that EXEMPTS cqrt_copy from the forward-consumer count re-opens the spurious-free / hidden-measurement bug — it is verify-clean and trace-plausible. Found by the WI-4 §8 adversarial review (2026-06-11): §6.2 originally credited only isTerminalHandle for out; HasFanOut-via-copy is the operative guard for the source-rooted dead chain. Probe: the no-spurious-free CHECK-COUNT-2/3 + trailing CHECK-NOT cqrt_free in control_swap_value_{diamond,ifelse}.ll.

Any new merge-φ-building detection path (BranchRegion via matchDiamond/matchSymmetricDiamond/matchNestedAnd, SwitchRegion via tryBuildGatedSwitchRegion) MUST guard its merge φ — a φ the reduction can't lower must DECLINE, never dangle. Two distinct discriminators, by path:

(1) BR-DIAMOND paths use the select-form B1 predicate (unlowerableClassicalMergePhi, ControlDetection.cpp): a wholly-classical (no-tainted-incoming) φ whose type can't be lowered = !isIntegerTy() || abiWidthFromType().empty(). PITFALL (cwk adversarial review 2026-06-02): a plain isFloatingPointTy() test is a TRAP — scalar-only (misses <2 x double>; use isFPOrFPVectorTy), ignores i128/odd-width/pointer φ. ROOT CAUSE of the f64 miscompile: reduceClassicalMux keys on abiWidthFromType non-empty, but f64 IS a valid DATA width, so it built cqrt_alloc_f64 + made the angle an i32 handle. Diamond classical-INTEGER φ (real data mux) DOES lower via reduceClassicalMux.

(2) GATED-SWITCH path: lowerGatedSwitch has NO data-mux lowering (no reduceClassicalMux) — step 4 dissolves a handle φ ONLY by RAUW to a tainted incoming, assuming EVERY incoming is the same in-place handle. So tryBuildGatedSwitchRegion (6qg, commit 4939d84) requires every non-angle merge φ to be UNIFORMLY tainted (all incomings tainted); ANY non-tainted incoming → decline to the WP12 'switch under quantum control' diagnostic. Adversarial review 2026-06-03 (6qg shared-arms) caught the too-weak first cut (declined only ALL-classical φ via 'AnyTainted'): a φ MIXING a tainted handle with classical constants (a gate arm that also assigns a classical value, e.g. phi[%v1,c1],[1000,c7],[2000,dflt]) slipped through, step-4 RAUW dropped the classical edges → returned the raw handle id (verify-clean silent miscompile). The all-tainted rule also closes the pre-existing all-classical-φ-in-gated-switch crash (<badref> φ → report_fatal_error) and is over-decline-safe (a value-propagated-constant-equal-to-handle is indistinguishable from a genuine distinct value, so declining is the only safe call — NEVER miscompile). THIRD tightening (npu.1, commit 21264b6, 2026-06-03): all-tainted was STILL too weak — it required all incomings tainted but NOT the same BASE handle. An all-tainted φ collecting DISTINCT per-case handles (case0→qx, case1→qy; a coherent quantum multiplexer) slipped through, and step-4 RAUW collapsed it to the FIRST incoming, silently DROPPING the other-handle edges (s==1 then operates on qx, not qy; verify-clean miscompile). NOW ENFORCED per-φ: resolveGatedHandleBase (ControlDetection.cpp) unwraps each incoming's cq_phi chain to its base handle; a φ with ≥2 distinct bases declines to WP12. The check is PER-φ — a genuine MULTI-handle merge keeps distinct handles on SEPARATE φs (each uniform in its own base), so _multihandle still lowers. INTERIM decline only; correct lowering of a distinct-handle multiplexer is the deferred Bennett MUX-EXCH / controlled-SWAP (cqrt_cswap) feature = npu.4 (primitive) → npu.5 (MUX-EXCH lowering) → npu.6 (non-selected-source uncompute); see [[tainted-arm-select-mux-no-new-primitive]] (reversed for the free-the-sources case). Regression fixtures: lowering_control_switch_gated_{datamux,mixedphi,distinct}.ll. Angle φ are exempt (recorded by classifyAngleMerge, lowered by reduceAngleSwitchPhi). Fix (b) angle lowering = [[byx]]. See [[angle-reducer-single-block-invariant]].

d3ji (store a quantum handle into a local scratch slot -> g7ip-sibling store->load forwarding) INVESTIGATED 2026-07-04, NOT built: the accept-shape is UNREACHABLE on the clang -O1 validated floor (Rule 9). FINDING: d3ji's forwarder would prove a scratch alloca slot single-write/single-read/no-alias/no-escape at a provably-identical CLASSICAL address, then RAUW the read-back load to the stored %out handle + erase the store/load (measure(load)->measure(%out)). But clang -O1's GVN/MemDep ALREADY forwards exactly this whenever it is provable, using full alias analysis + MemorySSA (STRICTLY STRONGER than d3ji's structural same-SSA-pointer proof). So d3ji's accept-set is a STRICT SUBSET of what GVN eliminates before the cq-lowering pass runs. A store->load round-trip survives -O1 ONLY when GVN cannot prove the addresses match -- which is EXACTLY when d3ji must ALSO decline (forwarding would silent-miscompile). Verified on 6 real -O1 emissions (scratchpad/d3ji/t*.c): same dynamic-arg index (literal pA1), single volatile-read index, struct field, asm memory barrier, distinct const slots -> ALL forwarded away by GVN, array/struct deleted, measure reads the phi directly (which dugh/6.5 then lowers correctly with NO d3ji). The ONLY survivor is arr[i]=y; load arr[j] with i,j two SEPARATE volatile reads (not provably equal) -> a DECLINE (forwarding wrong if i!=j), not an accept. CONTRAST g7ip (which DOES survive -O1): its store is in a non-inlined CALLEE and the load in the CALLER, straddling a call boundary GVN cannot see across; a SAME-FUNCTION local array has no such barrier so GVN sees both sides. CONSEQUENCE: a d3ji forwarder would be DEAD CODE on -O1 and cannot be exercised by an e2e golden (Rule-16 done-criterion; Rule-2 says hand-authored IR like pA1 is NOT correctness evidence). The current kMsgStore decline (control_classical_call_arm_reject_localarray_store.ll) fires ONLY on hand-authored off-floor IR and is a SAFE over-decline (Prime Directive) -- there is NO real -O1 input mishandled. RECOMMENDATION (pending owner, asked 2026-07-04, owner away): close d3ji as not-reachable/won't-fix and keep the safe decline; do NOT add unexercisable mutation code to the correctness-critical TaintPropagation.cpp core. Alt: rescope to the genuinely-different capability of a quantum handle stored then read at a QUANTUM index (superposition register-file, the dual of 7.5 Shadow, largely no-cloning-bound) -- NOT store->load forwarding. See [[dugh-second-propagation-round]] [[g7ip-inline-producer-design]]. Findings doc: docs/prd/phase-04-swap-route-control/d3ji-scratch-store-forward-PRD.md.

d8jl ('control flow inside a loop body' guard) was filed as diagnostic-accuracy but is a CORRECTNESS/ROBUSTNESS fix (closed 2026-06-30). ROOT CAUSE: detectControlRegions ACCEPTS-and-EMITS a flat tainted-condition diamond/if-else/switch AND a depth-2 nest INSIDE a loop body; RegionFlatten/flattenRegionTree then erases the merge block (= the loop LATCH / backedge source), dangling the loop header/re-entry phi -> BROKEN MODULE (opt SIGABRT 'PHI node entries do not match predecessors!') on REAL clang -O1 output of 'for(){int q=cq_theta(x,a); if(q>5)q=cq_phi(q,b); acc+=cq_measure(q);}'. The ITERATION-LOCAL shape (fresh cq_theta each iter, measured in-body, NOTHING tainted loop-carried) is the dangerous one: no surviving classical-mux phi, so the declineClassicalMuxes net that masked the loop-CARRIED shape (which mislabeled the QUANTUM cond as 'classical-condition phi') never fires -> straight to broken module. FIX: detect-before-flatten guard regionEntryInLoop(Instruction* Term) in ControlDetect.cpp -- a COMPLETE forward CFG reachability walk (does Term's block reach itself = on a cycle), wired into THREE dispatch arms: (1) br Diamond/IfElse arm before classifyClassicalCallArm/classifyArms -> 'control flow inside a loop body'; (2) switch dispatch before classifySwitchRegion -> 'control flow inside a loop body'; (3) RegionShape::Nested arm before recoverRegionTree -> 'nested control flow' (message preserved, no fixture churn). CRITICAL: the guard MUST be REDUCIBILITY-INDEPENDENT. LoopInfo/getLoopFor AND recoverRegionTree's own DT.dominates backedge test BOTH MISS irreducible loops (a goto-into-loop body / Duff's device, clang -O1 reachable: entry branches to TWO cycle blocks so no header dominates the cycle, getLoopFor==null, no edge tests as a backedge) -- those still broken-module'd and were found ONLY in adversarial review (Rule 13), never by the green suite. Do NOT use llvm::isPotentiallyReachable: it bails 'true' past a 32-block scan limit -> would over-decline a legit NON-loop diamond in a large function. The walk is EXACT: for a flat/nested/switch region the entry's ONLY successors are region blocks, so entry-reaches-itself <=> region-on-a-cycle (no spurious, no missed cycles); terminating (each block Seen once). NON-flatten paths are loop-safe and left alone: in-loop SELECT (4.4) is a benign verifier-clean exit-0 iteration-local accept (no CFG flatten); AbortParkEmit erases only the abort arm (never a merge); LoopLowering/BreakReversePlay erase phis/terminators not blocks (LoopInfo-gated, no-op on irreducible); break loops escape the guard because emitBreakForward rewrites the exit cond to the classical bound BEFORE detection. ONE intentional NARROWING (reviewer-approved): a REDUCIBLE external-latch iteration-local nest that previously lowered (UNVERIFIED, Phase-4.3-explicitly-out-of-scope, whose irreducible sibling crashed; recoverRegionTree's own comment flagged it 'do NOT over-trust') now declines uniformly -- Prime-Directive-safe. Fixtures: control_swap_reject_inloop_diamond{,_iterlocal,_irreducible}.ll, control_swap_reject_inloop_switch.ll, control_swap_reject_nested_loop_irreducible.ll. Rule 17 (CLAUDE.md, owner-added 2026-06-26) — Build the intent; a decline is not the DEVELOPMENT escape hatch. When the TASK is to implement support for a construct, attempt the real lowering; do NOT substitute a loud decline for the hard work, and do NOT reflexively gate the intended target shape behind an over-safe decline check. This does NOT weaken the Prime Directive at RUNTIME: a genuinely off-pattern / unprovable INPUT still declines loudly (over-accepting is still the one unforgivable silent miscompile; an over-safe decline of a shape we were NOT trying to support is still correct). The change is DEVELOPMENT POSTURE only. If the implementation proves genuinely difficult, ambiguous, or off-pattern in a way that tempts declining the very thing we aimed to build, STOP and bring questions/a discussion back to the owner rather than silently shipping a decline-only stub and calling it done. The decline belongs to inputs OUTSIDE the target shape, not to the target shape itself. Distinction vs Prime Directive: Prime Directive governs the lowered compiler's OUTPUT for unprovable inputs (unchanged); Rule 17 governs MY behavior while implementing a feature (don't punt to decline; escalate to owner when stuck).

FILECHECK TEST-RIGOR GOTCHA (found by Rule-13 fixture-rigor lens, bd 20xt.5.2, 2026-07-23): a CHECK-NOT block placed AFTER the last positive CHECK is VACUOUS — FileCheck scans a CHECK-NOT only over the region BETWEEN its neighbouring positive directives, so negatives appended after the final 'CHECK: ret ...' scan ONLY the trailing text (e.g. the module's declare/attributes tail), NEVER the function body they were meant to guard. WORSE in this pass's spec-clone fixtures: Phase-6 specialization leaves the DEAD un-lowered ORIGINAL callee (@lookup with its br/phi/load double/select) ABOVE the clone in the -S output, so a whole-output '--implicit-check-not=phi|br|select|load double' ALSO false-positives on that dead function. FIX: (1) 'CHECK-LABEL: define ... @__cq_q_<clone>' to anchor the clone; (2) INTERLEAVE each CHECK-NOT between two adjacent positive CHECKs that bracket the body region you want scanned (e.g. put 'CHECK-NOT: cqrt_free(i32 %[[ARR]])' between the last reverse 'CHECK: ...load_f64_unc' and 'CHECK: ret', so it scans the free region; put 'CHECK-NOT: br i1 / = phi / = select i1 / load double' between the read CHECK and the merge CHECK). VERIFY the negatives are non-vacuous by INJECTING the forbidden shape (perl -pe to splice 'cqrt_free(i32 %arr)' + 'br i1 ...' before the clone ret) and confirming FileCheck now EXITS 1. Applies to every spec_accept_*/control_*_accept fixture that asserts Rule-6/8 (array/result rail never freed) or 'control gone' negatives. See [[clone-control-qram-coherent-escape-20xt52]].

CQ_lang SCOPE SPLIT (taint-driven design, branch taint-driven-pipeline):

FRONTEND = CQ.h header + standard Clang invocation. The user #includes CQ.h, writes plain C with calls to cq_theta / cq_phi / cq_measure / cq_invert_begin/_end, and Clang -O1 -emit-llvm produces 'Stage 1' bitcode. Frontend deliverable: stock LLVM IR with @cq_theta_<sfx>, @cq_phi_<sfx>, @cq_measure_<sfx>, @cq_invert_begin/_end calls preserved as opaque externals; plain i1/i8/i16/i32/i64/f32/f64 SSA throughout; post-mem2reg, post-SROA. The frontend NEVER emits qint_mid_t, @cq_init_*, @cq_alloc_*, @cq_when_*, or any cqrt_* / cq_template_* call. There is NO rewriter — the prior libtooling transpiler is archived.

BACKEND = the IR pass (ir-pass/, built as plugin libCQPass.so loaded by 'opt -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-lowering') + libcq_runtime + libcq_templates. Pass responsibilities: (a) forward taint propagation from @cq_theta returns; (b) gate-triggered allocation insertion (cqrt_alloc_<W> before first cq_theta on classical operand); (c) opcode lowering of tainted stock LLVM ops into cq_template_<op>_<W>{,_hl} calls; (d) call-graph specialization (curated symbol substitution + clone-on-taint per backend.md §7); (e) controlled-form lowering via PostDominatorTree on tainted br i1; (f) per-op uncomputation at SSA last-use; (g) adjoint emission via emit_inverse; (h) manual inversion bracket substitution. Pass output: only cqrt_* runtime calls + cq_template_* template calls + stock classical SSA threading them — no @cq_* intrinsics remain.

WHEN DISCUSSING ARCHITECTURE: do NOT conflate the layers. The frontend NEVER emits cqrt_*, cq_template_*, or controlled-form variants — those are pass outputs. Three-stage flow: Stage 1 (clang -O1 -emit-llvm -include CQ.h) → Stage 2 (opt + cq-lowering pass) → Stage 3 (clang codegen + link -lcq_templates -lcq_runtime). See docs/frontend.md §8 and docs/backend.md §13 for full pipeline.

ROOT-CAUSE CLASS: a dyn_cast<CallInst> that DETECTS a front-end intrinsic or runtime call silently assumes a CallInst and returns null on an InvokeInst — an UNDER-taint silent gap. It hit collectAndSeed (invoke'd theta never seeded -> result treated CLASSICAL -> downstream tainted control that should decline never starts; @cq_* extern -> Stage-3 link error) and isMeasureSink (invoke'd measure not a sink -> over-taint through it). FIX PATTERN (decline, NOT lower-uniformly — an InvokeInst is a TERMINATOR with normal+unwind successors and every lowering stage inserts call-position CallInsts + RAUWs, so uniform lowering is unsafe terminator surgery): (1) collectAndSeed walks CallBase, declines any non-CallInst CallBase of an intrinsic via diagnoseIntrinsicInvoke ('cq taint propagation: front-end intrinsic <name> reached via invoke; only a direct call is supported'), records it in taint.IntrinsicInvokes, collects nothing; (2) isMeasureSink -> CallBase (defensive: invoke'd measure still a sink for any host that continues past the DS_Error); (3) declineTaintEscapes skips taint.IntrinsicInvokes by EXACT POINTER membership — NEVER name-prefix (a user fn named cq_theta_evil via invoke must still escape as unknown-callee) — to avoid a misleading double 'unknown callee'. Not reachable from the supported frontend (clang -O1, no exceptions, emits 'call' not 'invoke' for opaque externs) -> P3 robustness; no e2e possible, lit decline fixtures are the gate (lowering_reject_intrinsic_invoke_{theta,phi,measure}.ll).
