THE RULE-10 LESSON (why 2 approaches failed -- deep+interlocked): a folded bitcast makes result===operand (ONE physical wire). Approaches 1+2 KEPT the bitcast STANDING and tried to make each analysis CROSS it (WireWalk backward+forward identity-hop + checkStaleOp exemption). FAILED because the pass has MANY BESPOKE provenance/lineage walks that DO NOT share one walker: stale-record checkStaleOp AND its separate chained-theta-arg0 backward hop (WireWalk lines ~103), SelectClassify hasCoherentDownstreamUse/operandCarriesPhase (GATE 5), IOSink continued-lineage/terminality, ArmClassify wireGainsNonDiagonalGate, SwitchArmProve. Patching some left others BLIND -> 3 confirmed verify-clean SILENT-MISCOMPILE blockers, each 'folded form ACCEPTS but the DIRECT twin DECLINES': (a) %b=bitcast %q; %q2=cq_theta(%b,t2); sibling cq_theta(%q,t3); add %q2 -> add lowers over post-Ry basis; (b) tainted select value-operand = bitcast result over a re-rotated wire -> 4.4 controlled-XOR copy captures stale basis; (c) printf(bitcast result) over a re-rotated wire -> tape records stale wire. ALSO a Rule-17 OVER-DECLINE from an even-earlier position-free-for-bitcast attempt: it declined measure-after-rerotate, but a MEASURE reads the wire in place (base pass ACCEPTS cq_theta;cq_theta;measure(orig)). EARLY FOLDING dissolves ALL of it: no standing identity node => nothing for any walk to be blind to => reduces to base-pass behavior => any FUTURE bespoke walk is automatically safe. This is the freeze-fold precedent (declineTaintEscapes folds identity freezes early for the same reason).

SEMANTIC ANCHOR (base-pass, re-verifiable): DATA op reading a re-rotated wire DECLINES ('operand predates a non-diagonal gate'); MEASURE reading a re-rotated wire ACCEPTS (in-place, no fresh-rail capture). Bitcast form must match its direct twin exactly.

COMPLETENESS (why no straggler): propagate() conservatively taints EVERY user of a tainted value, incl. specialized-call results reading tainted args AND bitcasts thereof, BEFORE the fold; specialize() only SCRUBS taint (never adds); by-ref runs before the fold and doesn't create/touch int<->int bitcasts. So no tainted same-width int bitcast survives the fold to an analysis. Side-table hygiene: at fold time (before RotationLowering/lowerOps) ONLY Tainted holds the bitcast (Theta/Phi/MeasureCalls are CallInst-only; BirthOrder/HandleWidth/StaleDeclined/ControlOwnedRails all seeded later), so scrubbing Tainted+HandleWidth is sufficient. KNOWN SAFE nits (Prime-Directive over-declines, pre-existing, NOT iw81.1-introduced): a same-width int bitcast in a specialization CANDIDATE BODY or a by-ref PRODUCER BODY is UNtainted at fold time (callee param not taint-seeded) -> left standing -> scanBody:372 'pointer cast' / byref isPureValueOp reject it (direct twin accepts). i128<->i128 identity is fold-eligible+folds (a genuine bit-identity, harmless).

LIT-ONLY (no e2e): clang -O1 folds same-width int bitcasts BEFORE the pass, so the accept path is unconstructible in C. normalizeJumpTableAngle (SwitchNormalization.cpp, test_C_libtooling-5zu) rewrites the clang -O1 jump-table lowering of a tainted ANGLE switch — (idx<N)?table[idx]:base with idx=q+K, @table a constant double array — into the WP16 eq-flag angle-select chain (base + Σ_i [q==i−K]·(table[i]−base)) BEFORE detection, so reduceAngleSelectChain lowers it and the gep/load are gone before diagnoseTaintedMemoryEscape runs (no carve-out needed). It runs as a pre-pass in CQLoweringPass after normalizeTaintedSwitches. CONSERVATISM IS LOAD-BEARING (adversarial review 2026-06-03 found 4 over-match silent-miscompiles/broken-modules; recognizer must DECLINE any non-canonical shape so the memory-escape guard stays the safe fallback): (1) element type MUST be double (cq_phi/cqrt_rz angle is double-only for every width; an f32 table feeds a float to double-typed cqrt_rz = broken module); a non-FP/i32 table is DATA not angle. (2) Lookup arm must contain ONLY {optional zext/sext, gep, load, br} — DeleteDeadBlock erases the block, so any store/call/extra instr would be silently dropped. (3) load must be isSimple() (no volatile/atomic) AND hasOneUse() (the φ) — else a use beyond the φ strands a dangling ref. (4) gep/cast hasOneUse, gep 2-index with zero first index, constant global with initializer, single 2-incoming merge φ feeding only cq_phi angle args, tainted scrutinee, predicate ult with lookup=true-successor. Affine correctness: q↦q+K is a bijection mod 2^32 so {q:(q+K)∈[0,N)} == {i−K mod 2^32 : i∈[0,N)} (the eq constants) — exact even under unsigned wrap; the affine/decline-safety review dimensions found 0 issues. Regression fixtures: lowering_control_switch_jumptable{,_i32,_sideeffect,_loadreuse,_nonconst}.ll. See [[angle-reducer-single-block-invariant]].

The old math.h 165/174 (95%) was TEMPLATE-RECOGNITION = FICTION: once the source is injected the named call/intrinsic is inlined away to opcodes, so the recognizer never fires. SOLE EXCEPTION = HARDWARE-BACKED intrinsics: an intrinsic that codegens to a hardware instruction (or inline opcode sequence) with NO libcall has no injectable body -> recognized directly and KEPT. CRITERION (testable, TARGET-DEPENDENT, must MEASURE not guess -- Rule 11): compile T f(T x){return f(x);} at clang -O1; KEEP iff no external call/jmp to _<fn> (hardware/inline opcodes); CUT iff clang emits a libcall (call or tail-jmp _<fn>). EMPIRICAL KEEP-SET x86-64+SSE4.1 no-FMA3 (14): sqrt fabs copysign floor ceil trunc round rint nearbyint fmin fmax fma/fmuladd lrint llrint (+ the non-math integer bit-intrinsics bswap/ctpop/... untouched). RESOLVED 2026-07-06 (bd p119.8, DONE + Rule-13 CLEARED). The control-merge out-rail HandleWidth gap (a merge emitter not recording taint.HandleWidth[Out]=Abi, so a downstream cast/Q+Q-compare off the RAUW'd merge reads the laundered i32 and over-declines) is now FIXED in ALL FOUR merge emitters: SelectMergeEmit (p119.6), SwitchDataMuxEmit, SwitchValueEmit, ClassicalCallArmEmit (p119.8). Each adds taint.HandleWidth[Out]=Abi right after BirthOrder[Out], where Abi is the merge's own width (abiWidthFromType of the phi/select/chain type). SAFETY (cleared): Abi is definitionally == the merge's SSA type (no wrong-in-scope symbol); the write is strictly AFTER the copyFn/copyControlledFn null-fence (isIntegerTy && bitwidth<=64), so an fp/i128 merge declines loudly BEFORE Out is created -- no fp/i128 width is ever recorded; the only 2 HandleWidth readers (cast From-recovery OpcodeLowering:263, Q+Q compare agreement CompareLowering:315) both FAIL-SAFE (regression over-declines, never miscompiles); persists across the round-2 repropagateControlMerges (a plain side-table -- verified with an i8 data-mux whose cast lowers only in round 2). Pinned: lowering_switch_datamux_nonI32_cast.ll, lowering_switch_value_nonI32_cast.ll, control_classical_call_arm_accept_nonI32_cast.ll (i64 merge -> trunc each) + the p119.6 select fixtures. NOTE: an i8 classical-call ARM is NOT an accepted classifier shape (declines 'control flow under quantum control'); i64 IS -- the classical-call fixture uses i64. The producer invariant 'HandleWidth[v]==v result width' now holds for EVERY producer.

Mint-at-compare for the chained-Ry stale-condition shape (c=(q>5); q=cq_theta(q,t2); if(c){...}) is RESOLVED as a PERMANENT decline (test_C_libtooling-ee5, 2026-06-10; design-of-record docs/design/rssa-swap-control/MINT_AT_COMPARE.md, oracle investigation_mint_at_compare.py — all probes assert exact closed forms). THEOREM (P6): the source state |Psi> = |0>_f psi0 + |1>_f psi1 has MIXED rho_q (purity 1-2a^2b^2(1-|u|^2), u=cos(t2/2)sin(t2/2)(e^{ia}-1)), so ANY compilation that frees the flag ends |0>_f(x)|phi> with a PURE q-marginal — source-exactness and a freeable flag are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, ceiling sup|<Psi_src|0_f,phi>| = cos(gamma/2). Every candidate strip verified failing: naive icmp_inv residual sin^2(t2/2); Bennett conjugated strip Ry†;icmp_inv;Ry residual b^2 sin^2(t2)sin^2(a/2) (does not commute with the arm phase); full reverse-play strips clean but ERASES the arm (replayed CRz sees |0> control, fid cos^2(gamma/2)); t2=pi corner strips clean but answer lost; value-arm conjugated strip strips clean but coherently ERASES the icmp's record (record-merging interference separates 0.500 vs 0.946 — a clean flag is NOT evidence of soundness). The ONLY source-exact compilation LEAKS the entangled flag rail (fid 1.0 incl. downstream interference, rails still exactly |0>) — admissible under Rule 6 but REJECTED as a silent default (Rule 5 forward-only-mode precedent); recorded as future explicit opt-in only. SECOND FINDING (two guard holes, both fixed): (1) the original positional guard (scan [icmp,br) for tainted thetas) was UNSOUND under Rule 9 — a pure icmp SUNK below the chained theta (SSA unchanged, %c reads pre-Ry %q) was confirmed ACCEPTED+MISCOMPILED by the in-tree pass (mint after cqrt_ry(t2), verify-clean, stream fid cos^2(t2/2)=0.848); (2) the first wire-walk fix seeded only the compare's DIRECT tainted operands, so a DERIVED condition (%d=add %q,1; icmp %d — an accepted region shape TODAY) hid the stale %q one pure wire-hop away: confirmed ACCEPTED+MISCOMPILED (cq_template_add emitted post-Ry; found by ee5 round-2 review). Final fix in ArmClassify::wireGainsNonDiagonalGate: seed from the condition's full tainted backward PROVENANCE (condProvenance), follow cq_phi arg-0 user edges (same wire, diagonal), decline on any cq_theta arg-0 user. The walk does not cross the merge phi, so phi-mediated post-region thetas are unreachable; a DIRECT post-region theta user of a provenance value IS reachable and declines — over-decline, safe by design, do not 'fix'. Fixtures: control_swap_reject_stalecond_{chained_theta,sunk_compare,derived_cond}.ll. RESIDUAL: the same stale-record family with NO branch (straight-line q=theta(u0,g); q2=theta(q,t2); d=q+1; measure(d)) is silently accepted pass-wide (OpcodeLowering domain, outside ArmClassify's reach) — tracked as test_C_libtooling-uzb (P1 bug). GENERAL LESSON: pure instructions (icmp/add/cast) have NO reliable program point — only opaque cq_* call order is stable; any accept-predicate about 'when' a tainted pure value is evaluated must reason by SSA wire-window seeded from FULL provenance (direct operands are not the wire), never instruction position.

MINTER-NULL-IS-A-CLASSIFIER HAZARD (found by the 2026-07-02 fp-data-select PRD adversarial review, 47-agent workflow; the PRD's original §4.2 was a BLOCKER for this). In this codebase a symbol minter's null return is often the LIVE decline gate for a consumer, not mechanical plumbing: the 6.5 classical-call arm's ONLY fp/i128 fence is ControlledSymbols::copyControlledFn returning null (DD-7 — classifyClassicalCallArm at ArmClassify.cpp:1078-1189 has NO type/angle/coherence gate of its own; ArmClassify.cpp:1184-1185 + ClassicalCallArmEmit.cpp:102-113 explicitly delegate). CNOT-copying a cq_phi phase-carrier with no operandCarriesPhase check (the WI-3 dephasing family). RULE: before widening ANY shared minter (copyControlledFn / tapeWriteControlledFn / copyFn / allocFn...), enumerate ALL consumers and classify each fence as (a) upstream classifier gate (safe) or (b) minter-null-carried (the widening IS a classifier change there — add an explicit gate to that consumer in the same commit or mint via a separate local entry). 2026-07-02 consumer audit of copyControlledFn: SelectMergeEmit + SwitchDataMuxEmit + IOSinkLowering:655 + BreakReversePlay:208 all classifier-fenced (SwitchClassify G4; ArmClassify:853/:872; IOSink ConstantInt+i32 gates :218/:223/:503-505; LoopLowering opcode Add/Xor + isIntegerTy<=64 :133-145 + uncontrolled copyFn null :845-847); ClassicalCallArmEmit was the UNIQUE minter-null-fenced consumer. Resolution: fp select mints via a select-local copyControlledFpFn (fp-data-select-PRD §4.2 revised); copyControlledFn's integer fence stays byte-identical. Related tripwire: adding uncontrolled cqrt_copy_f<W> later flips ChainWalk.cpp:76-78 isCopyOutSink prefix-matching and LoopLowering's copyFn fence — re-audit both then.

MLIR adoption: EVALUATED AND REJECTED for v1 under the taint-driven design. The minimal user-facing surface — 4 intrinsic families (cq_theta, cq_phi, cq_measure, cq_invert_*), no custom quantum type, no quantum-specific arithmetic ops (stock LLVM opcodes throughout), allocation gate-triggered at IR-pass time, plain SSA at fn boundaries — collapses a would-be MLIR dialect to ~3 truly-quantum ops (theta, phi, measure) plus inversion-region markers, essentially identical to the intrinsic surface already declared in CQ.h. MLIR's ~6-8 week substrate cost outweighs its benefit for that surface; transformative benefits (type-enforced quantum-ness, region-based ops, multi-level lowering) only emerge when custom types/ops carry quantum semantics, which CQ deliberately does not adopt.

RE-EVALUATION GATE: deferred to Phase 10 freeze (ROADMAP.md §Phase 10, 'MLIR re-evaluation gate'). Re-trigger condition: did any IR-pass mechanism in Phases 2-7 demand an intra-dialect transformation the new PassManager cannot express cleanly? If yes, post-freeze scope expands to evaluate MLIR for a v2; if no, intrinsic + stock-LLVM is locked for v1.

HOW TO APPLY: future 'should we use MLIR?' questions should reference this decision and ROADMAP.md §Phase 10 trigger first. Detailed v1-era rationale preserved at docs/archive/old-design/architecture.md §11; do not cite that doc as live design.

MUX-EXCH distinct-base gated switch + non-linear handle use (test_C_libtooling-bqs, investigated+adversarially-confirmed 2026-06-03, CLOSED not-a-bug). A 'dead arm-local cq_phi on a mux base' is NOT a genuine miscompile: it requires using a handle SSA value twice as a gate operand (no-cloning/linearity violation) which the linear CQ.h frontend cannot emit. Under the IN-PLACE handle model rotation lowering RAUWs {q, cq_phi(q,.), .} to ONE i32 handle, so a non-linear dead-clone arm lowers BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the well-formed LINEAR two-gate arm (q->t->r1) — both become two cqrt_rz on the one register, the valid linear interpretation; the cswap captures all in-arm gates before the move, non-selected uncompute is balanced. Adversarial sweep (10 probe families) found NO accepted-and-miscompiled linear input; genuine cross-arm hazards over-decline via G3b (_wrongarmmut*), cross-φ/post-merge cloning via G6 (_crossphi_alias,_postmergelive). DESIGN STANCE: no general IR-level linearity checker — spec §1 is correctness-by-construction on linear well-formed input (frontend guarantees linearity; specific cloning shapes declined). Lock fixture: lowering_control_switch_gated_distinct_multigatearm.ll. See [[mux-exch-gate-per-arm-correspondence]], [[mux-exch-5bl-widening-nested-merge-guard]].

MUX-EXCH gated-switch lowering (npu.5/.6, ControlledLowering.cpp lowerGatedSwitch + ControlDetection.cpp muxBasePreconditions/muxRegionGate, gated by region.MuxExch). A distinct-per-case-handle merge phi lowers as regOut=cqrt_alloc(0) + per-distinct-base cqrt_cswap(f_q,regOut,q) MOVE + per-NON-selected-source cqrt_ry_<W>_controlled_inv(NOT f_q,q,angle) uncompute. The default-selected base's control is the COMPLEMENT of OtherCaseOr (OR of the other bases' case-flags) via a cqrt_x self-inverse bracket — the partition identity (exactly one arm fires), NOT an explicit NOT-OrAll value. A MuxAnchor (mirrors AngleAnchor) pins step-5 flag uncompute AFTER the mux body so the consumed flags stay live. CARDINAL G3 INVARIANT (adversarial review C1, 2026-06-03, confirmed silent miscompile): G3a 'every user of a mux base is an in-region gate body' (set-membership over region.Shadow + all SwitchArm.Shadow) is NOT sufficient — it admits a stray cq_phi(q,angle) sitting in a NON-q-selecting arm, whose cqrt_rz_controlled fires on a NOT-f_q branch; the single Ry-dagger uncompute cannot undo that stray Rz so q stays entangled with the scrutinee and regOut decoheres (verify-clean, trace runtime can't catch it). FIX = G3b per-arm correspondence: every gate mutating base q must live in an arm whose mux-phi edge carries q (Mux->getBasicBlockIndex(G->getParent()) then resolveGatedHandleBase(incoming)==resolveGatedHandleBase(G)), else decline to WP12. Regression fixtures lowering_control_switch_gated_distinct_wrongarmmut{,_default}.ll. Spec docs/npu6-mux-exch-gate-spec.md G3b. LAUNDER-BY-ERASURE has a hole at NON-ERASED tainted users — the broken-module-on-ACCEPT-input class (test_C_libtooling-udw, fixed 2026-06-11, cleared by 3-lens adversarial review). Every lowering path RAUWs an iN-typed tainted SSA value to an ALWAYS-i32 runtime handle (cqrt_alloc_*/cqrt_copy_* return i32; RotationLowering.cpp ~line174 RAUWs theta->i32 handle). The cross-type RAUW is well-typed ONLY because every tainted user is itself lowered+ERASED. A 'ret' user is NEVER erased, so returning a tainted value at a width OTHER than i32 ('ret i64 %q' straight-line; the phase-diamond merge ret; the value-diamond cqrt_copy merge ret which PRD Part II §8.5 sanctions as ACCEPT-class) leaves 'ret <iN!=32> <i32 handle>' -> verifier report_fatal_error('Broken module found'), opt exit 134. That is LOUD but UNCONSUMABLE and NOT the Rule-1 source-located decline — and for the value-diamond it crashes ACCEPT-class input. FIX: pre-RAUW guard in declineTaintEscapes (TaintPropagation.cpp section 4): 'if ReturnInst && Tainted.count(RV) && !RV->getType()->isIntegerTy(32) -> diagnoseEscape(kMsgNonI32Return)'. Same move as ArmClassify::taintedAngleGate ('declining here turns the later broken-module abort into a clean, source-located decline'). KEY: the guard keys on OPERAND TAINT not return width — a cq_measure result is the CLASSICAL taint SINK (untainted), so 'ret i64 %m' stays ACCEPTED (boundary fixture lowering_taint_escape_return_measure_i64.ll). i32 tainted rets stay accepted (FreePoint Escaped). The 'handle is ALWAYS i32' invariant makes isIntegerTy(32) decisive: a tainted non-i32 value can NEVER be well-typed at a ret. GENERAL LESSON: any time you RAUW a tainted value to the i32 handle and rely on erasure to launder the type, audit every NON-erased user class (ret today; future: any terminator/intrinsic the pass doesn't rewrite). Fixtures: lowering_reject_taint_escape_return_{straightline,phase_diamond,value_diamond}.ll.

Phase 4.5 WI-6 -O1 SHAPE REALITY (measured 2026-06-17 against clang -O1 on this tree, for the tainted-switch e2e goldens slice_control_switch_{phase,value,datamux,eqfold}.c): getting a C 'switch' to reach cq-lowering AS a real LLVM 'switch' (not folded to a select chain / lookup-table, not declined) is the hard part of e2e — the datamux/value .ll contracts are hand-written precisely because clang folds small const/arith switches. Recipe per ACCEPT class: (PHASE) homogeneous cq_phi arms survive NATURALLY (opaque call = unspeculatable, like 4.1) — switch(q){case 0:q=cq_phi(q,.1);case 1:...;case 2:...} stays a switch, and -O1 const-folds each arm gate's arg-0 to its case literal cq_phi(i32 c_i,θ) (the §5 re-anchor signature). (EQFOLD) if(q==7){2-gate phase} survives as a br-diamond; a SINGLE-gate arm canonicalizes to a tainted ANGLE select (4.4-deferred -> declines), so use >=2 gates. (VALUE) switch(q){case 0:p=p+1;case 1:p=p+2;} on a SEPARATE tainted base p!=q SURVIVES even with 2 single-add arms (non-const base p defeats the const-mux fold) — contrast [[o1-value-arm-select-folding]] where a SHORT if-arm folds to select; the switch is more fold-resistant. (DATAMUX) the killer: a const data-mux switch(q){case:r=const} FOLDS to a nested select chain. TWO tricks needed together: (a) NON-CONTIGUOUS case values (0/5/17, not 0/1/2) — defeats BOTH the select-fold (>2-3 distinct results) AND the lookup-table-fold (sparse range not beneficial); (b) PRE-INITIALIZE r=v_d before the switch and OMIT the explicit 'default:' body. QUANTUM-UB SHARP-EDGE for tainted-control 'unreachable'/UB-dead arms (bd 20xt.5 (d), Rule-13-noted 2026-07-18): when PredMux flattens a tainted-control region containing an 'unreachable' block (or drops a UB-dead arm), the soundness rests on the LLVM LangRef contract that reaching 'unreachable' is UB. Under a QUANTUM-SUPERPOSED tainted condition this is a genuine but SOUND sharp-edge: for a STRUCTURALLY-exhaustive default (clang proved exhaustiveness over ALL bit patterns, e.g. 'switch (q & 3)' over {0,1,2,3} — the atan2l quadrant shape) the default is unreachable on EVERY basis state, so zero trust needed. For a SOURCE-asserted default (__builtin_unreachable / __builtin_assume) a classically-dead branch may carry NONZERO amplitude on some basis-state component; the flatten then produces the select-chain FALLBACK value for that component. This is NOT a compiler miscompile: __builtin_unreachable is a UB contract binding the WHOLE superposition support (Rule 5), so a violating component is source-level UB and the compiler may produce any value; the flattened result is a SOUND TOTAL REFINEMENT of the source's PARTIAL unitary. Critically the coherence is preserved on the DEFINED support: the 4.4 select-merge ancilla uncompute (toffoli then inverse-toffoli / icmp _inv strip) restores every rail to |0> on EVERY basis state, so no dirty free / cross-basis collapse of the well-defined components. Same principle as the shipped Inc-3 QROM NeedsMask mask (OOB read is source-UB => obligation-free). RULE: trust valid input IR's UB markers (Rule 11); a tainted-control 'unreachable' is obligation-free to drop. See predmux-unreachable-default-20xt5-d.

ziov WI-1 (branch swap-route-control, 2026-06-15): a tainted control compare 'q>5' that clang -O1 CSEs into BOTH a 'br' (control) AND a data position ('int f=(q>5)') is now ACCEPTED on the FLAT phase-arm path by SHARING ONE flag — superseding the old blanket decline 'condition used outside the branch' (ArmClassify) which wrongly rejected valid code. MECHANISM: classifyArms.condDataUseDisposition(Cond, Region.Pred) decides ShareOk vs decline by a pure forward SSA walk of the compare's non-branch users (Rule 9). On ShareOk it sets Region.ShareCondFlag; emitRegion mints the flag ONCE at Cond->getNextNode() (so it dominates data uses that precede the routed stream), records taint.SharedCondFlags[Cond]=Flag (does NOT RAUW), and SKIPS the eager strip(icmp_inv)+free (steps 7-8) — the data lineage owns the handle. CompareLowering::rewriteCompare REUSES the recorded flag for the surviving data-position compare instead of minting a SECOND (the ziov duplicate-mint). Recording-not-RAUWing defers the cross-type i1->i32 launder to lowerOps Phase 2, AFTER Phase 1 captures the data casts' i1 source width (RAUWing in the emitter corrupts 'zext i1->i32' into a templateless 'zext i32->i32' — confirmed). emitValueRegion DECLINES ShareCondFlag (value-arm sharing = later WI); nested (RegionTreeDetect/NestedRouteEmit) never sets it (nested cond-datause still duplicate-mints a benign leaked flag — filed follow-up). WHY skip strip+free is CORRECT (not a leak compromise): f IS the entangled q>5; STRIPPING would disentangle f from q and BE the miscompile. Cleared Rule-13 TWICE (4-lens find + 2-lens fix re-review). ziov WI-1 shared-condition-flag: the Rule-13 adversarial review (2026-06-15) found TWO verify-clean silent miscompiles in the FIRST-cut condDataUseDisposition that ALL green tests missed — both now guarded + pinned by decline fixtures. (A) MEASURE-BEFORE-ROUTE: 'bool f=cq_measure(q>5); if(q>5){...}' — clang -O1 puts the cq_measure of the flag in the PRED (route) block, BEFORE the cswap route is emitted (route lands at IRBuilder(BI), BI=Region.Pred->terminator). Sharing+skip-strip then emits cqrt_measure on the flag BEFORE the route's cswap, so the route is controlled by an ALREADY-COLLAPSED flag -> coherent if(q>5) control silently destroyed. GUARD: a cq_measure_/cqrt_measure_ user of the flag lineage whose getParent()==RouteBlock(=Region.Pred) -> decline 'condition measured before the control route'. A measure DOWNSTREAM (merge block) is fine (post-route). Sound because cross-block-Cond declines via nonDiagonalGateBeforeBranch first, and SSA dominance forbids a flag-lineage measure in a block dominating Pred. Fixture control_swap_reject_cond_datause_measure_early.ll. (B) MAIN-NAME SHORT-CIRCUIT: an 'if (getName()=="main") return true' accepted ANY data lineage in main incl. a DEAD one that the non-main path declines as a Rule 6/8 dirty-entangled-flag hazard — disposition keyed on a string, not lineage ownership. FreePoint's main rule governs the FREE question ONLY, never the strip/coherence question. GUARD: removed the short-circuit; condDataUseDisposition walks identically regardless of function name (dead-in-main declines 'condition data use neither escaped nor measured'). Fixture control_swap_reject_cond_datause_main_dead.ll. LESSON: a measure/escape 'owns' a shared quantum flag only when ORDERED AFTER the control use; ownership is about coherence+position, not just reachability. Also: cq_invert removed from accept set (un-laundered i1->i32 RAUW could break the module on a non-i32 param). See [[ziov-wi1-shared-condition-flag]].

ziov.2 (branch swap-route-control, 2026-06-15): WI-2's proposed accept of the DEAD-within-function cond-data-use phase region — share one flag, emit a DEFERRED icmp_inv strip + cqrt_free at the post-dom of all flag uses (reuse FreePoint + WireWalk), strip the FLAG ONLY — was REVIEWED (4-lens adversarial workflow + refutations + synthesis, all high-confidence, zero facts refuted) and CLOSED won't-fix-as-specified. It is a verify-clean SILENT MISCOMPILE. WHY: every data-op template mints a FRESH rail (runtime/cq_templates.c: cq_template_zext/add -> cqrt_alloc_handle), so 'int f=(q>5); dead=f+7' beside if(q>5){rz} produces COPIES d=zext(q>5), dead=add(d,7) entangled with q. A flag-ONLY deferred strip returns the flag to |0> but never touches d/dead. Statevector: after route+Rz+route-back (work rail back to |0>), state is (|0>q|0>d + e^{i.theta}|1>q|1>d)/sqrt2; strip flag only -> q stays tied to d; tracing out d (orthogonal records) DESTROYS q off-diagonal coherence = q dephased as if measured, the arm phase lost under any later interference (Grover/QPE). SCOPING 3a flag-strip is coherent ONLY when the flag is the SOLE ancilla; leaked d=q>5 is the which-region/dephasing class (3 line 184, Rule 8), NOT Rule 6 benign disentangled leak. Existing uncompute spine CANNOT clean d/dead: ChainWalk recoverForwardChain hits the shared flag which fans out to the route cswaps (forwardConsumerCount counts cswap) -> HasFanOut -> Uncomputation isStep2Emittable=false -> skipped (emitInverseChain always Flag=nullptr; taint.ControlFlag never written, FlagImage empty). ALSO unreachable from clang -O1: a truly-dead tainted lineage is fully DCE'd to bare 'icmp; br' (verified by compiling the fixture C); a lineage kept live by a store is constant-folded to a branch-keyed phi OR declined earlier as a tainted-store escape — so 'survives -O1' and 'dead/unowned tainted lineage rooted at the control compare' are contradictory. DISPOSITION: keep declining PERMANENTLY (ArmClassify CondDataDisp::Unowned -> 'condition data use neither escaped nor measured'). A CORRECT accept would need NEW fan-out-aware data-lineage uncompute: route-back, reverse-play dead then d to |0> (reads the flag, BEFORE the flag strip), free d/dead rails, then the SINGLE icmp_inv flag strip once, free flag — substantial core lowering (Rule 13 zone) with the shared-prefix double-uncompute hazard (Rule 8), for ZERO real-program coverage — not built. Comments retargeted in ArmClassify.cpp/ControlPlan.h/SwapRouteEmit.cpp + fixture headers control_swap_reject_cond_datause_dead.ll and _nested_cond_datause_dead.ll. See [[ziov-wi1-shared-condition-flag]] [[ziov-wi1-two-silent-miscompiles]].
